     410  static int write_credential(
     411                  int dfd,
     412                  const char *id,
     413                  const void *data,
     414                  size_t size,
     415                  uid_t uid,
     416                  gid_t gid,
     417                  bool ownership_ok) {
     418  
     419          _cleanup_close_ int fd = -EBADF;
     420          int r;
     421  
     422          assert(dfd >= 0);
     423          assert(id);
     424          assert(data || size == 0);
     425  
     426          fd = openat(dfd, id, O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY|O_CLOEXEC, 0600);
     427          if (fd < 0)
     428                  return -errno;
     429  
     430          r = loop_write(fd, data, size);
     431          if (r < 0)
     432                  return r;
     433  
     434          r = RET_NERRNO(fchmod(fd, 0400)); /* Take away "w" bit */
     435          if (r < 0)
     436                  return r;
     437  
     438          if (uid_is_valid(uid) && uid != getuid()) {
     439                  r = fd_add_uid_acl_permission(fd, uid, ACL_READ);
     440                  /* Ideally we use ACLs, since we can neatly express what we want to express:
     441                   * the user gets read access and nothing else. But if the backing fs can't
     442                   * support that (e.g. ramfs), then we can use file ownership instead. But that's
     443                   * only safe if we can then re-mount the whole thing read-only, so that the user
     444                   * can no longer chmod() the file to gain write access. */
     445                  if ((ERRNO_IS_NEG_NOT_SUPPORTED(r) || ERRNO_IS_NEG_PRIVILEGE(r)) && ownership_ok)
     446                          r = RET_NERRNO(fchown(fd, uid, gid));
     447                  if (r < 0)
     448                          return r;
     449          }
     450  
     451          return 0;
     452  }

     454  static int maybe_decrypt_and_write_credential(
     455                  LoadCredentialArguments *args,

     471                  CredentialFlags flags = 0; /* only allow user creds in user scope */
     472  
     473                  switch (args->context->scope) {
     474  
     475                  case RUNTIME_SCOPE_SYSTEM:
     476                          /* In system mode talk directly to the TPM – unless we live in a device sandbox
     477                           * which might block TPM device access. */
     478  
     479                          flags |= CREDENTIAL_ANY_SCOPE;
     480  
     481                          if (!args->context->always_ipc) {
     482                                  r = decrypt_credential_and_warn(

     484                                                  now(CLOCK_REALTIME),

     487                                                  getuid(),
     488                                                  &IOVEC_MAKE(data, size),
     489                                                  flags,

     492                          }

     494                          _fallthrough_;
     495  
     496                  case RUNTIME_SCOPE_USER:

     498                           * likely), hence go via the IPC service instead. Do this if we are run in root's
     499                           * per-user invocation too, to minimize differences and because isolating this logic
     500                           * into a separate process is generally a good thing anyway. */
     501                          r = ipc_decrypt_credential(
     502                                          id,
     503                                          now(CLOCK_REALTIME),
     504                                          getuid(),
     505                                          &IOVEC_MAKE(data, size),
     506                                          flags,
     507                                          &plaintext);
     508                          break;
     509  
     510                  default:
     511                          assert_not_reached();
     512                  }
     513                  if (r < 0) {
     514                          if (graceful) {
     515                                  log_warning_errno(r, "Unable to decrypt credential '%s', skipping: %m", id);

     517                          }
     518  
     519                          return r;
     520                  }

     522                  data = plaintext.iov_base;

     530          r = write_credential(args->write_dfd, id, data, size, args->context->uid, args->context->gid, args->ownership_ok);

     532                  return log_debug_errno(r, "Failed to write credential '%s': %m", id);
     533  
     534          args->left -= add;
     535  
     536          return 0;
     537  }

     614  
     615          return 0;
     616  }
     617  
     618  static int load_credential(
     619                  LoadCredentialArguments *args,
     620                  const char *id,
     621                  int read_dfd,
     622                  const char *path) {
     623  
     624          ReadFullFileFlags flags = READ_FULL_FILE_SECURE|READ_FULL_FILE_FAIL_WHEN_LARGER;
     625          _cleanup_strv_free_ char **search_path = NULL;
     626          _cleanup_free_ char *bindname = NULL;
     627          const char *source = NULL;
     628          bool missing_ok;
     629          _cleanup_(erase_and_freep) char *data = NULL;
     630          size_t size, maxsz;
     631          int r;
     632  
     633          assert(args);
     634          assert(args->context);
     635          assert(args->context->exec_context);
     636          assert(args->context->unit);
     637          assert(id);
     638          assert(read_dfd >= 0 || read_dfd == AT_FDCWD);
     639          assert(path);
     640  
     641          if (read_dfd >= 0) {
     642                  /* If a directory fd is specified, then read the file directly from that dir. In this case we
     643                   * won't do AF_UNIX stuff (we simply don't want to recursively iterate down a tree of AF_UNIX
     644                   * IPC sockets). It's OK if a file vanishes here in the time we enumerate it and intend to
     645                   * open it. */
     646  
     647                  if (!filename_is_valid(path)) /* safety check */
     648                          return -EINVAL;
     649  
     650                  missing_ok = true;
     651                  source = path;
     652  
     653          } else if (path_is_absolute(path)) {
     654                  /* If this is an absolute path, read the data directly from it, and support AF_UNIX
     655                   * sockets */
     656  
     657                  if (!path_is_valid(path)) /* safety check */
     658                          return -EINVAL;
     659  
     660                  flags |= READ_FULL_FILE_CONNECT_SOCKET;
     661  
     662                  /* Pass some minimal info about the unit and the credential name we are looking to acquire
     663                   * via the source socket address in case we read off an AF_UNIX socket. */
     664                  if (asprintf(&bindname, "@%" PRIx64 "/unit/%s/%s", random_u64(), args->context->unit, id) < 0)
     665                          return -ENOMEM;
     666  
     667                  missing_ok = false;
     668                  source = path;
     669  
     670          } else if (credential_name_valid(path)) {
     671                  /* If this is a relative path, take it as credential name relative to the credentials
     672                   * directory we received ourselves. We don't support the AF_UNIX stuff in this mode, since we
     673                   * are operating on a credential store, i.e. this is guaranteed to be regular files. */
     674  
     675                  r = credential_search_path(args->context, CREDENTIAL_SEARCH_PATH_ALL, &search_path);
     676                  if (r < 0)
     677                          return r;
     678  
     679                  missing_ok = true;
     680          } else
     681                  return -EINVAL;
     682  
     683          if (args->encrypted) {
     684                  flags |= READ_FULL_FILE_UNBASE64;
     685                  maxsz = CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTED_SIZE_MAX;
     686          } else
     687                  maxsz = CREDENTIAL_SIZE_MAX;
     688  
     689          if (search_path)
     690                  STRV_FOREACH(d, search_path) {
     691                          _cleanup_free_ char *j = NULL;
     692  
     693                          j = path_join(*d, path);
     694                          if (!j)
     695                                  return -ENOMEM;
     696  
     697                          r = read_full_file_full(
     698                                          AT_FDCWD, j, /* path is absolute, hence pass AT_FDCWD as nop dir fd here */
     699                                          UINT64_MAX,
     700                                          maxsz,
     701                                          flags,
     702                                          NULL,
     703                                          &data, &size);
     704                          if (r != -ENOENT)
     705                                  break;
     706                  }
     707          else if (source)
     708                  r = read_full_file_full(
     709                                  read_dfd, source,
     710                                  UINT64_MAX,
     711                                  maxsz,
     712                                  flags,
     713                                  bindname,
     714                                  &data, &size);
     715          else
     716                  assert_not_reached();
     717  
     718          if (r == -ENOENT) {
     719                  bool in_set_credentials = hashmap_contains(args->context->exec_context->set_credentials, id);
     720                  if (missing_ok || in_set_credentials) {
     721                          /* Make a missing inherited credential non-fatal, let's just continue. After all apps
     722                           * will get clear errors if we don't pass such a missing credential on as they
     723                           * themselves will get ENOENT when trying to read them, which should not be much
     724                           * worse than when we handle the error here and make it fatal.
     725                           *
     726                           * Also, if the source file doesn't exist, but a fallback is set via SetCredentials=
     727                           * we are fine, too. */
     728                          log_full_errno(in_set_credentials ? LOG_DEBUG : LOG_INFO,
     729                                         r, "Couldn't read inherited credential '%s', skipping: %m", path);
     730                          return 0;
     731                  }
     732          }
     733          if (r < 0)
     734                  return log_debug_errno(r, "Failed to read credential '%s': %m", path);
     735  
     736          return maybe_decrypt_and_write_credential(args, id, data, size, /* graceful= */ false);
     737  }
     738  
     739  static int load_cred_recurse_dir_cb(
     740                  RecurseDirEvent event,
     741                  const char *path,
     742                  int dir_fd,
     743                  int inode_fd,
     744                  const struct dirent *de,
     745                  const struct statx *sx,
     746                  void *userdata) {
     747  
     748          LoadCredentialArguments *args = ASSERT_PTR(userdata);
     749          _cleanup_free_ char *sub_id = NULL;
     750          int r;
     751  
     752          assert(path);
     753          assert(de);
     754  
     755          if (event != RECURSE_DIR_ENTRY)
     756                  return RECURSE_DIR_CONTINUE;
     757  
     758          if (!IN_SET(de->d_type, DT_REG, DT_SOCK))
     759                  return RECURSE_DIR_CONTINUE;
     760  
     761          sub_id = strreplace(path, "/", "_");
     762          if (!sub_id)
     763                  return -ENOMEM;
     764  
     765          if (!credential_name_valid(sub_id))
     766                  return log_debug_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EINVAL), "Credential would get ID '%s', which is not valid, refusing.", sub_id);
     767  
     768          if (faccessat(args->write_dfd, sub_id, F_OK, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) >= 0) {
     769                  log_debug("Skipping credential with duplicated ID %s at %s", sub_id, path);
     770                  return RECURSE_DIR_CONTINUE;
     771          }
     772          if (errno != ENOENT)
     773                  return log_debug_errno(errno, "Failed to test if credential %s exists: %m", sub_id);
     774  
     775          r = load_credential(args,
     776                              sub_id,
     777                              dir_fd, de->d_name);
     778          if (r < 0)
     779                  return r;
     780  
     781          return RECURSE_DIR_CONTINUE;
     782  }
     783  
     784  static bool device_nodes_restricted(
     785                  const ExecContext *c,
     786                  const CGroupContext *cgroup_context) {
     787  
     788          assert(c);
     789          assert(cgroup_context);
     790  
     791          /* Returns true if we have any reason to believe we might not be able to access the TPM device
     792           * directly, even if we run as root/PID 1. This could be because /dev/ is replaced by a private
     793           * version, or because a device node access list is configured. */
     794  
     795          if (c->private_devices)
     796                  return true;
     797  
     798          if (cgroup_context_has_device_policy(cgroup_context))
     799                  return true;
     800  
     801          return false;
     802  }
     803  
     804  static int acquire_credentials(
     805                  const SetupCredentialsContext *context,
     806                  int dfd,
     807                  bool ownership_ok) {
     808  
     809          int r;
     810  
     811          assert(context);
     812          assert(context->exec_context);
     813          assert(dfd >= 0);
     814  
     815          LoadCredentialArguments args = {
     816                  .context = context,
     817  
     818                  .write_dfd = dfd,
     819                  .ownership_ok = ownership_ok,
     820                  .left = CREDENTIALS_TOTAL_SIZE_MAX,
     821          };
     822  
     823          /* First, load credentials off disk (or acquire via AF_UNIX socket) */
     824          ExecLoadCredential *lc;
     825          HASHMAP_FOREACH(lc, context->exec_context->load_credentials) {
     826                  _cleanup_close_ int sub_fd = -EBADF;
     827  
     828                  args.encrypted = lc->encrypted;
     829  
     830                  /* If this is an absolute path, then try to open it as a directory. If that works, then we'll
     831                   * recurse into it. If it is an absolute path but it isn't a directory, then we'll open it as
     832                   * a regular file. Finally, if it's a relative path we will use it as a credential name to
     833                   * propagate a credential passed to us from further up. */
     834  
     835                  if (path_is_absolute(lc->path)) {
     836                          sub_fd = open(lc->path, O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC);
     837                          if (sub_fd < 0 && !IN_SET(errno,
     838                                                    ENOTDIR,  /* Not a directory */
     839                                                    ENOENT))  /* Doesn't exist? */
     840                                  return log_debug_errno(errno, "Failed to open credential source '%s': %m", lc->path);
     841                  }
     842  
     843                  if (sub_fd < 0)
     844                          /* Regular file (incl. a credential passed in from higher up) */
     845                          r = load_credential(&args,
     846                                              lc->id,
     847                                              AT_FDCWD, lc->path);
     848                  else
     849                          /* Directory */
     850                          r = recurse_dir(sub_fd,
     851                                          /* path= */ lc->id, /* recurse_dir() will suffix the subdir paths from here to the top-level id */
     852                                          /* statx_mask= */ 0,
     853                                          /* n_depth_max= */ UINT_MAX,
     854                                          RECURSE_DIR_SORT|RECURSE_DIR_IGNORE_DOT|RECURSE_DIR_ENSURE_TYPE,
     855                                          load_cred_recurse_dir_cb,
     856                                          &args);
     857                  if (r < 0)
     858                          return r;
     859          }
     860  
     861          /* Next, look for system credentials and credentials in the credentials store. Note that these do not
     862           * override any credentials found earlier. */
     863          ExecImportCredential *ic;
     864          ORDERED_SET_FOREACH(ic, context->exec_context->import_credentials) {
     865                  _cleanup_free_ char **search_path = NULL;
     866  
     867                  r = credential_search_path(context, CREDENTIAL_SEARCH_PATH_TRUSTED, &search_path);
     868                  if (r < 0)
     869                          return r;
     870  
     871                  args.encrypted = false;
     872  
     873                  r = load_credential_glob(
     874                                  &args,
     875                                  ic,
     876                                  search_path,
     877                                  READ_FULL_FILE_SECURE|READ_FULL_FILE_FAIL_WHEN_LARGER);
     878                  if (r < 0)
     879                          return r;
     880  
     881                  search_path = strv_free(search_path);
     882  
     883                  r = credential_search_path(context, CREDENTIAL_SEARCH_PATH_ENCRYPTED, &search_path);
     884                  if (r < 0)
     885                          return r;
     886  
     887                  args.encrypted = true;
     888  
     889                  r = load_credential_glob(
     890                                  &args,
     891                                  ic,
     892                                  search_path,
     893                                  READ_FULL_FILE_SECURE|READ_FULL_FILE_FAIL_WHEN_LARGER|READ_FULL_FILE_UNBASE64);
     894                  if (r < 0)
     895                          return r;
     896          }
     897  
     898          /* Finally, we add in literally specified credentials. If the credentials already exist, we'll not
     899           * add them, so that they can act as a "default" if the same credential is specified multiple times. */
     900          ExecSetCredential *sc;
     901          HASHMAP_FOREACH(sc, context->exec_context->set_credentials) {
     902                  args.encrypted = sc->encrypted;
     903  
     904                  if (faccessat(dfd, sc->id, F_OK, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) >= 0) {
     905                          log_debug("Skipping credential with duplicated ID %s", sc->id);
     906                          continue;
     907                  }
     908                  if (errno != ENOENT)
     909                          return log_debug_errno(errno, "Failed to test if credential %s exists: %m", sc->id);
     910  
     911                  r = maybe_decrypt_and_write_credential(&args, sc->id, sc->data, sc->size, /* graceful= */ false);
     912                  if (r < 0)
     913                          return r;
     914          }
     915  
     916          return 0;
     917  }
     918  
     919  static int credentials_dir_finalize_permissions(int dfd, uid_t uid, gid_t gid, bool ownership_ok) {
     920          int r;
     921  
     922          assert(dfd >= 0);
     923  
     924          r = fd_acl_make_read_only(dfd); /* Take away the "w" bit */
     925          if (r < 0)
     926                  return r;
     927  
     928          /* After we created all keys with the right perms, also make sure the credential store as a whole is
     929           * accessible */
     930  
     931          if (uid_is_valid(uid) && uid != getuid()) {
     932                  r = fd_add_uid_acl_permission(dfd, uid, ACL_READ | ACL_EXECUTE);
     933                  if (r < 0) {
     934                          if (!ERRNO_IS_NOT_SUPPORTED(r) && !ERRNO_IS_PRIVILEGE(r))
     935                                  return r;
     936  
     937                          if (!ownership_ok)
     938                                  return r;
     939  
     940                          if (fchown(dfd, uid, gid) < 0)
     941                                  return -errno;
     942                  }
     943          }
     944  
     945          return 0;
     946  }
     947  
     948  static int setup_credentials_plain_dir(
     949                  const SetupCredentialsContext *context,
     950                  const char *cred_dir) {
     951  
     952          _cleanup_free_ char *t = NULL, *workspace = NULL;
     953          _cleanup_(rm_rf_safep) const char *workspace_rm = NULL;
     954          _cleanup_close_ int dfd = -EBADF;
     955          int r;
     956  
     957          assert(context);
     958          assert(context->unit);
     959          assert(context->runtime_prefix);
     960          assert(cred_dir);
     961  
     962          /* Temporary workspace, that remains inaccessible all the time. We prepare stuff there before moving
     963           * it into place, so that users can't access half-initialized credential stores. */
     964          t = path_join(context->runtime_prefix, "systemd/temporary-credentials");
     965          if (!t)
     966                  return -ENOMEM;
     967  
     968          r = mkdir_label(t, 0700);
     969          if (r < 0 && r != -EEXIST)
     970                  return r;
     971  
     972          workspace = path_join(t, context->unit);
     973          if (!workspace)
     974                  return -ENOMEM;
     975  
     976          dfd = open_mkdir(workspace, O_CLOEXEC|O_EXCL, 0700);
     977          if (dfd < 0)
     978                  return log_debug_errno(dfd, "Failed to create workspace for credentials: %m");
     979          workspace_rm = workspace;
     980  
     981          (void) label_fix_full(dfd, /* inode_path= */ NULL, cred_dir, /* flags= */ 0);
     982  
     983          r = acquire_credentials(context, dfd, /* ownership_ok= */ false);
     984          if (r < 0)
     985                  return r;
     986  
     987          r = RET_NERRNO(rename(workspace, cred_dir));
     988          if (r >= 0)
     989                  workspace_rm = NULL;
     990          if (IN_SET(r, -ENOTEMPTY, -EEXIST)) {
     991                  _cleanup_close_ int old_dfd = open(cred_dir, O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW);
     992                  if (old_dfd < 0)
     993                          return log_debug_errno(errno, "Failed to open credentials dir '%s': %m", cred_dir);
     994  
     995                  (void) fd_acl_make_writable(old_dfd);
     996  
     997                  log_debug_errno(r, "Credential dir '%s' already populated, exchanging with workspace.", cred_dir);
     998                  r = RET_NERRNO(renameat2(AT_FDCWD, workspace, AT_FDCWD, cred_dir, RENAME_EXCHANGE));
     999          }
    1000          if (r < 0)
    1001                  return log_debug_errno(r, "Failed to move credentials workspace into place: %m");
    1002  
    1003          /* rename() requires both the source and target to be writable, hence lock down write permission
    1004           * as last step. */
    1005          r = credentials_dir_finalize_permissions(dfd, context->uid, context->gid, /* ownership_ok= */ false);
    1006          if (r < 0)
    1007                  return log_debug_errno(r, "Failed to adjust ACLs of credentials dir: %m");
    1008  
    1009          return 0;
    1010  }
    1011  
    1012  static int setup_credentials_internal(
    1013                  const SetupCredentialsContext *context,
    1014                  bool may_reuse,
    1015                  const char *cred_dir) {
    1016  
    1017          _cleanup_close_ int fs_fd = -EBADF, mfd = -EBADF, dfd = -EBADF;
    1018          bool dir_mounted;
    1019          int r;
    1020  
    1021          assert(context);
    1022          assert(cred_dir);
    1023  
    1024          r = path_is_mount_point(cred_dir);
    1025          if (r < 0)
    1026                  return log_debug_errno(r, "Failed to determine if '%s' is a mountpoint: %m", cred_dir);
    1027          dir_mounted = r > 0;
    1028  
    1029          if (may_reuse) {
    1030                  bool populated;
    1031  
    1032                  /* If the cred dir is a mount, let's treat it as populated, and only look at the contents
    1033                   * if it's a plain dir, where we can't reasonably differentiate populated yet empty vs
    1034                   * not set up. */
    1035  
    1036                  if (dir_mounted)
    1037                          populated = true;
    1038                  else {
    1039                          r = dir_is_empty(cred_dir, /* ignore_hidden_or_backup= */ false);
    1040                          if (r < 0)
    1041                                  return r;
    1042                          populated = r == 0;
    1043                  }
    1044                  if (populated) {
    1045                          log_debug("Credential dir for unit '%s' already set up, skipping.", context->unit);
    1046                          return 0;
    1047                  }
    1048          }
    1049  
    1050          mfd = fsmount_credentials_fs(&fs_fd);
    1051          if (ERRNO_IS_NEG_PRIVILEGE(mfd) && !dir_mounted) {
    1052                  log_debug_errno(mfd, "Lacking privilege to mount credentials fs, falling back to plain directory.");
    1053                  return setup_credentials_plain_dir(context, cred_dir);
    1054          }
    1055          if (mfd < 0)
    1056                  return log_debug_errno(mfd, "Failed to mount credentials fs: %m");
    1057  
    1058          dfd = fd_reopen(mfd, O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC);
    1059          if (dfd < 0)
    1060                  return dfd;
    1061  
    1062          (void) label_fix_full(dfd, /* inode_path= */ NULL, cred_dir, /* flags= */ 0);
    1063  
    1064          r = acquire_credentials(context, dfd, /* ownership_ok= */ true);
    1065          if (r < 0)
    1066                  return r;
    1067  
    1068          r = credentials_dir_finalize_permissions(dfd, context->uid, context->gid, /* ownership_ok= */ true);
    1069          if (r < 0)
    1070                  return log_debug_errno(r, "Failed to adjust ACLs of credentials dir: %m");
    1071  
    1072          // Work around a kernel bug that results in tmpfs reconfiguration failure.
    1073          // FIXME: drop this once https://lore.kernel.org/linux-fsdevel/20251108190930.440685-1-me@yhndnzj.com/
    1074          // is merged and hits the distro kernels.
    1075          (void) fsconfig(fs_fd, FSCONFIG_SET_FLAG, "noswap", NULL, 0);
    1076  
    1077          if (fsconfig(fs_fd, FSCONFIG_SET_FLAG, "ro", NULL, 0) < 0)
    1078                  return -errno;
    1079  
    1080          if (fsconfig(fs_fd, FSCONFIG_CMD_RECONFIGURE, NULL, NULL, 0) < 0)
    1081                  return -errno;
    1082  
    1083          log_debug("Successfully reconfigured credentials fs to be read only.");
    1084  
    1085          if (dir_mounted) {
    1086                  /* Firstly, try to move beneath the existing mount, which guarantees strictly atomic replacement
    1087                   * (needs kernel >= 6.5) */
    1088                  r = move_mount(mfd, "", AT_FDCWD, cred_dir, MOVE_MOUNT_F_EMPTY_PATH|MOVE_MOUNT_BENEATH);
    1089                  if (r >= 0)
    1090                          return umount_verbose(LOG_DEBUG, cred_dir, MNT_DETACH|UMOUNT_NOFOLLOW);
    1091                  if (errno != EINVAL)
    1092                          return log_debug_errno(errno, "Failed to move credentials fs into place: %m");
    1093  
    1094                  log_debug_errno(errno, "Unable to move credentials fs beneath existing mount '%s', unmounting instead: %m",
    1095                                  cred_dir);
    1096  
    1097                  r = umount_verbose(LOG_DEBUG, cred_dir, MNT_DETACH|UMOUNT_NOFOLLOW);
    1098                  if (r < 0)
    1099                          return r;
    1100          }
    1101  
    1102          r = move_mount(mfd, "", AT_FDCWD, cred_dir, MOVE_MOUNT_F_EMPTY_PATH);
    1103          if (r < 0)
    1104                  return log_debug_errno(errno, "Failed to move credentials fs into place: %m");
    1105  
    1106          return 0;
    1107  }
    1108  
    1109  int exec_setup_credentials(
    1110                  const ExecContext *context,
    1111                  const CGroupContext *cgroup_context,
    1112                  const ExecParameters *params,
    1113                  uid_t uid,
    1114                  gid_t gid) {
    1115  
    1116          _cleanup_free_ char *p = NULL, *q = NULL;
    1117          int r;
    1118  
    1119          assert(context);
    1120          assert(params);
    1121  
    1122          if (!exec_params_need_credentials(params) || !exec_context_has_credentials(context))
    1123                  return 0;
    1124  
    1125          if (!params->prefix[EXEC_DIRECTORY_RUNTIME])
    1126                  return -EINVAL;
    1127  
    1128          /* This is where we'll place stuff when we are done; the main credentials directory is world-readable,
    1129           * and the subdir we mount over with a read-only file system readable by the service's user. */
    1130          q = path_join(params->prefix[EXEC_DIRECTORY_RUNTIME], "credentials");
    1131          if (!q)
    1132                  return -ENOMEM;
    1133  
    1134          r = mkdir_label(q, 0755); /* top-level dir: world readable/searchable */
    1135          if (r < 0 && r != -EEXIST)
    1136                  return r;
    1137  
    1138          p = path_join(q, params->unit_id);
    1139          if (!p)
    1140                  return -ENOMEM;
    1141  
    1142          r = mkdir_label(p, 0700); /* per-unit dir: private to user */
    1143          if (r < 0 && r != -EEXIST)
    1144                  return r;
    1145  
    1146          SetupCredentialsContext ctx = {
    1147                  .scope = params->runtime_scope,
    1148                  .exec_context = context,
    1149                  .unit = params->unit_id,
    1150  
    1151                  .runtime_prefix = params->prefix[EXEC_DIRECTORY_RUNTIME],
    1152                  .received_credentials_directory = params->received_credentials_directory,
    1153                  .received_encrypted_credentials_directory = params->received_encrypted_credentials_directory,
    1154  
    1155                  .always_ipc = device_nodes_restricted(context, cgroup_context),
    1156  
    1157                  .uid = uid,
    1158                  .gid = gid,
    1159          };
    1160  
    1161          r = setup_credentials_internal(&ctx, /* may_reuse = */ !FLAGS_SET(params->flags, EXEC_SETUP_CREDENTIALS_FRESH), p);
    1162          if (r < 0)
    1163                  (void) rmdir(p);
    1164  
    1165          return r;
    1166  }
    1167  
    1168  static int refresh_credentials_in_namespace_child(int cfd, const char *cred_dir) {
    1169          int r;
    1170  
    1171          assert(cfd >= 0);
    1172          assert(cred_dir);
    1173  
    1174          /* Paranoia: before doing anything, check if the credentials tree inside the mountns is available.
    1175           *

     402                  _cleanup_free_ char *t = strv_join(l, ":");
     403                  log_debug("Credential search path is: %s", strempty(t));
     404          }
     405  
     406          *ret = TAKE_PTR(l);
     407          return 0;
     408  }
     409  
     410  static int write_credential(
     411                  int dfd,
     412                  const char *id,
     413                  const void *data,
     414                  size_t size,
     415                  uid_t uid,
     416                  gid_t gid,
     417                  bool ownership_ok) {
     418  
     419          _cleanup_close_ int fd = -EBADF;
     420          int r;
     421  
     422          assert(dfd >= 0);
     423          assert(id);
     424          assert(data || size == 0);
     425  
     426          fd = openat(dfd, id, O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY|O_CLOEXEC, 0600);
     427          if (fd < 0)
     428                  return -errno;
     429  
     430          r = loop_write(fd, data, size);
     431          if (r < 0)
     432                  return r;
     433  
     434          r = RET_NERRNO(fchmod(fd, 0400)); /* Take away "w" bit */
     435          if (r < 0)
     436                  return r;
     437  
     438          if (uid_is_valid(uid) && uid != getuid()) {
     439                  r = fd_add_uid_acl_permission(fd, uid, ACL_READ);
     440                  /* Ideally we use ACLs, since we can neatly express what we want to express:
     441                   * the user gets read access and nothing else. But if the backing fs can't
     442                   * support that (e.g. ramfs), then we can use file ownership instead. But that's
     443                   * only safe if we can then re-mount the whole thing read-only, so that the user
     444                   * can no longer chmod() the file to gain write access. */
     445                  if ((ERRNO_IS_NEG_NOT_SUPPORTED(r) || ERRNO_IS_NEG_PRIVILEGE(r)) && ownership_ok)
     446                          r = RET_NERRNO(fchown(fd, uid, gid));
     447                  if (r < 0)
     448                          return r;
     449          }
     450  
     451          return 0;
     452  }
     453  
     454  static int maybe_decrypt_and_write_credential(
     455                  LoadCredentialArguments *args,
     456                  const char *id,
     457                  const char *data,
     458                  size_t size,
     459                  bool graceful) {
     460  
     461          _cleanup_(iovec_done_erase) struct iovec plaintext = {};
     462          size_t add;
     463          int r;
     464  
     465          assert(args);
     466          assert(args->write_dfd >= 0);
     467          assert(id);
     468          assert(data || size == 0);
     469  
     470          if (args->encrypted) {
     471                  CredentialFlags flags = 0; /* only allow user creds in user scope */
     472  
     473                  switch (args->context->scope) {
     474  
     475                  case RUNTIME_SCOPE_SYSTEM:
     476                          /* In system mode talk directly to the TPM – unless we live in a device sandbox
     477                           * which might block TPM device access. */
     478  
     479                          flags |= CREDENTIAL_ANY_SCOPE;
     480  
     481                          if (!args->context->always_ipc) {
     482                                  r = decrypt_credential_and_warn(
     483                                                  id,
     484                                                  now(CLOCK_REALTIME),
     485                                                  /* tpm2_device= */ NULL,
     486                                                  /* tpm2_signature_path= */ NULL,
     487                                                  getuid(),
     488                                                  &IOVEC_MAKE(data, size),
     489                                                  flags,
     490                                                  &plaintext);
     491                                  break;
     492                          }
     493  
     494                          _fallthrough_;
     495  
     496                  case RUNTIME_SCOPE_USER:
     497                          /* In per user mode we'll not have access to the machine secret, nor to the TPM (most
     498                           * likely), hence go via the IPC service instead. Do this if we are run in root's
     499                           * per-user invocation too, to minimize differences and because isolating this logic
     500                           * into a separate process is generally a good thing anyway. */
     501                          r = ipc_decrypt_credential(
     502                                          id,
     503                                          now(CLOCK_REALTIME),
     504                                          getuid(),
     505                                          &IOVEC_MAKE(data, size),
     506                                          flags,
     507                                          &plaintext);
     508                          break;
     509  
     510                  default:
     511                          assert_not_reached();
     512                  }
     513                  if (r < 0) {
     514                          if (graceful) {
     515                                  log_warning_errno(r, "Unable to decrypt credential '%s', skipping: %m", id);
     516                                  return 0;
     517                          }
     518  
     519                          return r;
     520                  }
     521  
     522                  data = plaintext.iov_base;
     523                  size = plaintext.iov_len;
     524          }
     525  
     526          add = strlen(id) + size;
     527          if (add > args->left)
     528                  return -E2BIG;
     529  
     530          r = write_credential(args->write_dfd, id, data, size, args->context->uid, args->context->gid, args->ownership_ok);
     531          if (r < 0)
     532                  return log_debug_errno(r, "Failed to write credential '%s': %m", id);
     533  
     534          args->left -= add;
     535  
     536          return 0;
     537  }
     538  
     539  static int load_credential_glob(
     540                  LoadCredentialArguments *args,
     541                  const ExecImportCredential *ic,
     542                  char * const *search_path,
     543                  ReadFullFileFlags flags) {
     544  
     545          int r;
     546  
     547          assert(args);
     548          assert(args->write_dfd >= 0);
     549          assert(ic);
     550          assert(search_path);
     551  
     552          STRV_FOREACH(d, search_path) {
     553                  _cleanup_strv_free_ char **paths = NULL;
     554                  _cleanup_free_ char *j = NULL;
     555  
     556                  j = path_join(*d, ic->glob);
     557                  if (!j)
     558                          return -ENOMEM;
     559  
     560                  r = safe_glob(j, /* flags= */ 0, &paths);
     561                  if (r == -ENOENT)
     562                          continue;
     563                  if (r < 0)
     564                          return r;
     565  
     566                  STRV_FOREACH(p, paths) {
     567                          _cleanup_free_ char *fn = NULL;
     568                          _cleanup_(erase_and_freep) char *data = NULL;
     569                          size_t size;
     570  
     571                          r = path_extract_filename(*p, &fn);
     572                          if (r < 0)
     573                                  return log_debug_errno(r, "Failed to extract filename from '%s': %m", *p);
     574  
     575                          if (ic->rename) {
     576                                  _cleanup_free_ char *renamed = NULL;
     577  
     578                                  renamed = strjoin(ic->rename, fn + strlen(ic->glob) - !!endswith(ic->glob, "*"));
     579                                  if (!renamed)
     580                                          return log_oom_debug();
     581  
     582                                  free_and_replace(fn, renamed);
     583                          }
     584  
     585                          if (!credential_name_valid(fn)) {
     586                                  log_debug("Skipping credential with invalid name: %s", fn);
     587                                  continue;
     588                          }
     589  
     590                          if (faccessat(args->write_dfd, fn, F_OK, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) >= 0) {
     591                                  log_debug("Skipping credential with duplicated ID %s at %s", fn, *p);
     592                                  continue;
     593                          }
     594                          if (errno != ENOENT)
     595                                  return log_debug_errno(errno, "Failed to test if credential %s exists: %m", fn);
     596  
     597                          /* path is absolute, hence pass AT_FDCWD as nop dir fd here */
     598                          r = read_full_file_full(
     599                                          AT_FDCWD,
     600                                          *p,
     601                                          UINT64_MAX,
     602                                          args->encrypted ? CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTED_SIZE_MAX : CREDENTIAL_SIZE_MAX,
     603                                          flags,
     604                                          NULL,
     605                                          &data, &size);
     606                          if (r < 0)
     607                                  return log_debug_errno(r, "Failed to read credential '%s': %m", *p);
     608  
     609                          r = maybe_decrypt_and_write_credential(args, fn, data, size, /* graceful= */ true);
     610                          if (r < 0)
     611                                  return r;
     612                  }
     613          }
     614  
     615          return 0;
     616  }
     617  
     618  static int load_credential(
     619                  LoadCredentialArguments *args,
     620                  const char *id,
     621                  int read_dfd,
     622                  const char *path) {
     623  
     624          ReadFullFileFlags flags = READ_FULL_FILE_SECURE|READ_FULL_FILE_FAIL_WHEN_LARGER;
     625          _cleanup_strv_free_ char **search_path = NULL;
     626          _cleanup_free_ char *bindname = NULL;
     627          const char *source = NULL;
     628          bool missing_ok;
     629          _cleanup_(erase_and_freep) char *data = NULL;
     630          size_t size, maxsz;
     631          int r;
     632  
     633          assert(args);
     634          assert(args->context);
     635          assert(args->context->exec_context);
     636          assert(args->context->unit);
     637          assert(id);
     638          assert(read_dfd >= 0 || read_dfd == AT_FDCWD);
     639          assert(path);
     640  
     641          if (read_dfd >= 0) {
     642                  /* If a directory fd is specified, then read the file directly from that dir. In this case we
     643                   * won't do AF_UNIX stuff (we simply don't want to recursively iterate down a tree of AF_UNIX
     644                   * IPC sockets). It's OK if a file vanishes here in the time we enumerate it and intend to
     645                   * open it. */
     646  
     647                  if (!filename_is_valid(path)) /* safety check */
     648                          return -EINVAL;
     649  
     650                  missing_ok = true;
     651                  source = path;
     652  
     653          } else if (path_is_absolute(path)) {
     654                  /* If this is an absolute path, read the data directly from it, and support AF_UNIX
     655                   * sockets */
     656  
     657                  if (!path_is_valid(path)) /* safety check */
     658                          return -EINVAL;
     659  
     660                  flags |= READ_FULL_FILE_CONNECT_SOCKET;
     661  
     662                  /* Pass some minimal info about the unit and the credential name we are looking to acquire
     663                   * via the source socket address in case we read off an AF_UNIX socket. */
     664                  if (asprintf(&bindname, "@%" PRIx64 "/unit/%s/%s", random_u64(), args->context->unit, id) < 0)
     665                          return -ENOMEM;
     666  
     667                  missing_ok = false;
     668                  source = path;
     669  
     670          } else if (credential_name_valid(path)) {
     671                  /* If this is a relative path, take it as credential name relative to the credentials
     672                   * directory we received ourselves. We don't support the AF_UNIX stuff in this mode, since we
     673                   * are operating on a credential store, i.e. this is guaranteed to be regular files. */
     674  
     675                  r = credential_search_path(args->context, CREDENTIAL_SEARCH_PATH_ALL, &search_path);
     676                  if (r < 0)
     677                          return r;
     678  
     679                  missing_ok = true;
     680          } else
     681                  return -EINVAL;
     682  
     683          if (args->encrypted) {
     684                  flags |= READ_FULL_FILE_UNBASE64;
     685                  maxsz = CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTED_SIZE_MAX;
     686          } else
     687                  maxsz = CREDENTIAL_SIZE_MAX;
     688  
     689          if (search_path)
     690                  STRV_FOREACH(d, search_path) {
     691                          _cleanup_free_ char *j = NULL;
     692  
     693                          j = path_join(*d, path);
     694                          if (!j)
     695                                  return -ENOMEM;
     696  
     697                          r = read_full_file_full(
     698                                          AT_FDCWD, j, /* path is absolute, hence pass AT_FDCWD as nop dir fd here */
     699                                          UINT64_MAX,
     700                                          maxsz,
     701                                          flags,
     702                                          NULL,
     703                                          &data, &size);
     704                          if (r != -ENOENT)
     705                                  break;
     706                  }
     707          else if (source)
     708                  r = read_full_file_full(
     709                                  read_dfd, source,
     710                                  UINT64_MAX,
     711                                  maxsz,
     712                                  flags,
     713                                  bindname,
     714                                  &data, &size);
     715          else
     716                  assert_not_reached();
     717  
     718          if (r == -ENOENT) {
     719                  bool in_set_credentials = hashmap_contains(args->context->exec_context->set_credentials, id);
     720                  if (missing_ok || in_set_credentials) {
     721                          /* Make a missing inherited credential non-fatal, let's just continue. After all apps
     722                           * will get clear errors if we don't pass such a missing credential on as they
     723                           * themselves will get ENOENT when trying to read them, which should not be much
     724                           * worse than when we handle the error here and make it fatal.
     725                           *
     726                           * Also, if the source file doesn't exist, but a fallback is set via SetCredentials=
     727                           * we are fine, too. */
     728                          log_full_errno(in_set_credentials ? LOG_DEBUG : LOG_INFO,
     729                                         r, "Couldn't read inherited credential '%s', skipping: %m", path);
     730                          return 0;
     731                  }
     732          }
     733          if (r < 0)
     734                  return log_debug_errno(r, "Failed to read credential '%s': %m", path);
     735  
     736          return maybe_decrypt_and_write_credential(args, id, data, size, /* graceful= */ false);
     737  }
     738  
     739  static int load_cred_recurse_dir_cb(
     740                  RecurseDirEvent event,
     741                  const char *path,
     742                  int dir_fd,
     743                  int inode_fd,
     744                  const struct dirent *de,
     745                  const struct statx *sx,
     746                  void *userdata) {
     747  
     748          LoadCredentialArguments *args = ASSERT_PTR(userdata);
     749          _cleanup_free_ char *sub_id = NULL;
     750          int r;
     751  
     752          assert(path);
     753          assert(de);
     754  
     755          if (event != RECURSE_DIR_ENTRY)
     756                  return RECURSE_DIR_CONTINUE;
     757  
     758          if (!IN_SET(de->d_type, DT_REG, DT_SOCK))
     759                  return RECURSE_DIR_CONTINUE;
     760  
     761          sub_id = strreplace(path, "/", "_");
     762          if (!sub_id)
     763                  return -ENOMEM;
     764  
     765          if (!credential_name_valid(sub_id))
     766                  return log_debug_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EINVAL), "Credential would get ID '%s', which is not valid, refusing.", sub_id);
     767  
     768          if (faccessat(args->write_dfd, sub_id, F_OK, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) >= 0) {
     769                  log_debug("Skipping credential with duplicated ID %s at %s", sub_id, path);
     770                  return RECURSE_DIR_CONTINUE;
     771          }
     772          if (errno != ENOENT)
     773                  return log_debug_errno(errno, "Failed to test if credential %s exists: %m", sub_id);
     774  
     775          r = load_credential(args,
     776                              sub_id,
     777                              dir_fd, de->d_name);
     778          if (r < 0)
     779                  return r;
     780  
     781          return RECURSE_DIR_CONTINUE;
     782  }
     783  
     784  static bool device_nodes_restricted(
     785                  const ExecContext *c,
     786                  const CGroupContext *cgroup_context) {
     787  
     788          assert(c);
     789          assert(cgroup_context);
     790  
     791          /* Returns true if we have any reason to believe we might not be able to access the TPM device
     792           * directly, even if we run as root/PID 1. This could be because /dev/ is replaced by a private
     793           * version, or because a device node access list is configured. */
     794  
     795          if (c->private_devices)
     796                  return true;
     797  
     798          if (cgroup_context_has_device_policy(cgroup_context))
     799                  return true;
     800  
     801          return false;
     802  }
     803  
     804  static int acquire_credentials(
     805                  const SetupCredentialsContext *context,
     806                  int dfd,
     807                  bool ownership_ok) {
     808  
     809          int r;
     810  
     811          assert(context);
     812          assert(context->exec_context);
     813          assert(dfd >= 0);
     814  
     815          LoadCredentialArguments args = {
     816                  .context = context,
     817  
     818                  .write_dfd = dfd,
     819                  .ownership_ok = ownership_ok,
     820                  .left = CREDENTIALS_TOTAL_SIZE_MAX,
     821          };
     822  
     823          /* First, load credentials off disk (or acquire via AF_UNIX socket) */
     824          ExecLoadCredential *lc;
     825          HASHMAP_FOREACH(lc, context->exec_context->load_credentials) {
     826                  _cleanup_close_ int sub_fd = -EBADF;
     827  
     828                  args.encrypted = lc->encrypted;
     829  
     830                  /* If this is an absolute path, then try to open it as a directory. If that works, then we'll
     831                   * recurse into it. If it is an absolute path but it isn't a directory, then we'll open it as
     832                   * a regular file. Finally, if it's a relative path we will use it as a credential name to
     833                   * propagate a credential passed to us from further up. */
     834  
     835                  if (path_is_absolute(lc->path)) {
     836                          sub_fd = open(lc->path, O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC);
     837                          if (sub_fd < 0 && !IN_SET(errno,
     838                                                    ENOTDIR,  /* Not a directory */
     839                                                    ENOENT))  /* Doesn't exist? */
     840                                  return log_debug_errno(errno, "Failed to open credential source '%s': %m", lc->path);
     841                  }
     842  
     843                  if (sub_fd < 0)
     844                          /* Regular file (incl. a credential passed in from higher up) */
     845                          r = load_credential(&args,
     846                                              lc->id,
     847                                              AT_FDCWD, lc->path);
     848                  else
     849                          /* Directory */
     850                          r = recurse_dir(sub_fd,
     851                                          /* path= */ lc->id, /* recurse_dir() will suffix the subdir paths from here to the top-level id */
     852                                          /* statx_mask= */ 0,
     853                                          /* n_depth_max= */ UINT_MAX,
     854                                          RECURSE_DIR_SORT|RECURSE_DIR_IGNORE_DOT|RECURSE_DIR_ENSURE_TYPE,
     855                                          load_cred_recurse_dir_cb,
     856                                          &args);
     857                  if (r < 0)
     858                          return r;
     859          }
     860  
     861          /* Next, look for system credentials and credentials in the credentials store. Note that these do not
     862           * override any credentials found earlier. */
     863          ExecImportCredential *ic;
     864          ORDERED_SET_FOREACH(ic, context->exec_context->import_credentials) {
     865                  _cleanup_free_ char **search_path = NULL;
     866  
     867                  r = credential_search_path(context, CREDENTIAL_SEARCH_PATH_TRUSTED, &search_path);
     868                  if (r < 0)
     869                          return r;
     870  
     871                  args.encrypted = false;
     872  
     873                  r = load_credential_glob(
     874                                  &args,
     875                                  ic,
     876                                  search_path,
     877                                  READ_FULL_FILE_SECURE|READ_FULL_FILE_FAIL_WHEN_LARGER);
     878                  if (r < 0)
     879                          return r;
     880  
     881                  search_path = strv_free(search_path);
     882  
     883                  r = credential_search_path(context, CREDENTIAL_SEARCH_PATH_ENCRYPTED, &search_path);
     884                  if (r < 0)
     885                          return r;
     886  
     887                  args.encrypted = true;
     888  
     889                  r = load_credential_glob(
     890                                  &args,
     891                                  ic,
     892                                  search_path,
     893                                  READ_FULL_FILE_SECURE|READ_FULL_FILE_FAIL_WHEN_LARGER|READ_FULL_FILE_UNBASE64);
     894                  if (r < 0)
     895                          return r;
     896          }
     897  
     898          /* Finally, we add in literally specified credentials. If the credentials already exist, we'll not
     899           * add them, so that they can act as a "default" if the same credential is specified multiple times. */
     900          ExecSetCredential *sc;
     901          HASHMAP_FOREACH(sc, context->exec_context->set_credentials) {
     902                  args.encrypted = sc->encrypted;
     903  
     904                  if (faccessat(dfd, sc->id, F_OK, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) >= 0) {
     905                          log_debug("Skipping credential with duplicated ID %s", sc->id);
     906                          continue;
     907                  }
     908                  if (errno != ENOENT)
     909                          return log_debug_errno(errno, "Failed to test if credential %s exists: %m", sc->id);
     910  
     911                  r = maybe_decrypt_and_write_credential(&args, sc->id, sc->data, sc->size, /* graceful= */ false);
     912                  if (r < 0)
     913                          return r;
     914          }
     915  
     916          return 0;
     917  }
     918  
     919  static int credentials_dir_finalize_permissions(int dfd, uid_t uid, gid_t gid, bool ownership_ok) {
     920          int r;
     921  
     922          assert(dfd >= 0);
     923  
     924          r = fd_acl_make_read_only(dfd); /* Take away the "w" bit */
     925          if (r < 0)
     926                  return r;
     927  
     928          /* After we created all keys with the right perms, also make sure the credential store as a whole is
     929           * accessible */
     930  
     931          if (uid_is_valid(uid) && uid != getuid()) {
     932                  r = fd_add_uid_acl_permission(dfd, uid, ACL_READ | ACL_EXECUTE);
     933                  if (r < 0) {
     934                          if (!ERRNO_IS_NOT_SUPPORTED(r) && !ERRNO_IS_PRIVILEGE(r))
     935                                  return r;
     936  
     937                          if (!ownership_ok)
     938                                  return r;
     939  
     940                          if (fchown(dfd, uid, gid) < 0)
     941                                  return -errno;
     942                  }
     943          }
     944  
     945          return 0;
     946  }
     947  
     948  static int setup_credentials_plain_dir(
     949                  const SetupCredentialsContext *context,
     950                  const char *cred_dir) {
     951  
     952          _cleanup_free_ char *t = NULL, *workspace = NULL;
     953          _cleanup_(rm_rf_safep) const char *workspace_rm = NULL;
     954          _cleanup_close_ int dfd = -EBADF;
     955          int r;
     956  
     957          assert(context);
     958          assert(context->unit);
     959          assert(context->runtime_prefix);
     960          assert(cred_dir);
     961  
     962          /* Temporary workspace, that remains inaccessible all the time. We prepare stuff there before moving
     963           * it into place, so that users can't access half-initialized credential stores. */
     964          t = path_join(context->runtime_prefix, "systemd/temporary-credentials");
     965          if (!t)
     966                  return -ENOMEM;
     967  
     968          r = mkdir_label(t, 0700);
     969          if (r < 0 && r != -EEXIST)
     970                  return r;
     971  
     972          workspace = path_join(t, context->unit);
     973          if (!workspace)
     974                  return -ENOMEM;
     975  
     976          dfd = open_mkdir(workspace, O_CLOEXEC|O_EXCL, 0700);
     977          if (dfd < 0)
     978                  return log_debug_errno(dfd, "Failed to create workspace for credentials: %m");
     979          workspace_rm = workspace;
     980  
     981          (void) label_fix_full(dfd, /* inode_path= */ NULL, cred_dir, /* flags= */ 0);
     982  
     983          r = acquire_credentials(context, dfd, /* ownership_ok= */ false);
     984          if (r < 0)
     985                  return r;
     986  
     987          r = RET_NERRNO(rename(workspace, cred_dir));
     988          if (r >= 0)
     989                  workspace_rm = NULL;
     990          if (IN_SET(r, -ENOTEMPTY, -EEXIST)) {
     991                  _cleanup_close_ int old_dfd = open(cred_dir, O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW);
     992                  if (old_dfd < 0)
     993                          return log_debug_errno(errno, "Failed to open credentials dir '%s': %m", cred_dir);
     994  
     995                  (void) fd_acl_make_writable(old_dfd);
     996  
     997                  log_debug_errno(r, "Credential dir '%s' already populated, exchanging with workspace.", cred_dir);

     303  static int request_parse_accept(
     304                  RequestMeta *m,
     305                  struct MHD_Connection *connection) {
     306  
     307          const char *header;

     309          assert(m);

     311  
     312          header = MHD_lookup_connection_value(connection, MHD_HEADER_KIND, "Accept");
     313          if (!header)
     314                  return 0;
     315  
     316          if (streq(header, mime_types[OUTPUT_JSON]))
     317                  m->mode = OUTPUT_JSON;
     318          else if (streq(header, mime_types[OUTPUT_JSON_SSE]))
     319                  m->mode = OUTPUT_JSON_SSE;
     320          else if (streq(header, mime_types[OUTPUT_JSON_SEQ]))
     321                  m->mode = OUTPUT_JSON_SEQ;
     322          else if (streq(header, mime_types[OUTPUT_EXPORT]))
     323                  m->mode = OUTPUT_EXPORT;
     324          else
     325                  m->mode = OUTPUT_SHORT;
     326  
     327          return 0;
     328  }

     331                  RequestMeta *m,
     332                  const char *colon) {

     338          if (colon2) {
     339                  _cleanup_free_ char *t = NULL;
     340  
     341                  t = strndup(colon + 1, colon2 - colon - 1);

     346                  if (r < 0)

     350          p = (colon2 ?: colon) + 1;

     362          return 0;

     629          size_t j;
     630  
     631          eq = memchr(d, '=', l);
     632          if (!eq)
     633                  return -EINVAL;
     634  
     635          j = l - (eq - d + 1);
     636  
     637          if (m == OUTPUT_JSON) {
     638                  fprintf(f, "{ \"%.*s\" : ", (int) (eq - d), d);
     639                  json_escape(f, eq+1, j, OUTPUT_FULL_WIDTH);
     640                  fputs(" }\n", f);
     641          } else {
     642                  fwrite(eq+1, 1, j, f);
     643                  fputc('\n', f);
     644          }
     645  
     646          return 0;
     647  }
     648  
     649  static ssize_t request_reader_fields(
     650                  void *cls,
     651                  uint64_t pos,
     652                  char *buf,
     653                  size_t max) {
     654  
     655          RequestMeta *m = ASSERT_PTR(cls);
     656          int r;
     657          size_t n, k;
     658  
     659          assert(buf);
     660          assert(max > 0);
     661          assert(pos >= m->delta);
     662  
     663          pos -= m->delta;
     664  
     665          while (pos >= m->size) {
     666                  off_t sz;
     667                  const void *d;
     668                  size_t l;
     669  
     670                  /* End of this field, so let's serialize the next
     671                   * one */
     672  
     673                  r = sd_journal_enumerate_unique(m->journal, &d, &l);
     674                  if (r < 0) {
     675                          log_error_errno(r, "Failed to advance field index: %m");
     676                          return MHD_CONTENT_READER_END_WITH_ERROR;
     677                  } else if (r == 0)
     678                          return MHD_CONTENT_READER_END_OF_STREAM;
     679  
     680                  pos -= m->size;
     681                  m->delta += m->size;
     682  
     683                  r = request_meta_ensure_tmp(m);
     684                  if (r < 0) {
     685                          log_error_errno(r, "Failed to create temporary file: %m");
     686                          return MHD_CONTENT_READER_END_WITH_ERROR;
     687                  }
     688  
     689                  r = output_field(m->tmp, m->mode, d, l);
     690                  if (r < 0) {
     691                          log_error_errno(r, "Failed to serialize item: %m");
     692                          return MHD_CONTENT_READER_END_WITH_ERROR;
     693                  }
     694  
     695                  sz = ftello(m->tmp);
     696                  if (sz < 0) {
     697                          log_error_errno(errno, "Failed to retrieve file position: %m");
     698                          return MHD_CONTENT_READER_END_WITH_ERROR;
     699                  }
     700  
     701                  m->size = (uint64_t) sz;
     702          }
     703  
     704          if (fseeko(m->tmp, pos, SEEK_SET) < 0) {
     705                  log_error_errno(errno, "Failed to seek to position: %m");
     706                  return MHD_CONTENT_READER_END_WITH_ERROR;
     707          }
     708  
     709          n = m->size - pos;
     710          if (n > max)
     711                  n = max;
     712  
     713          errno = 0;
     714          k = fread(buf, 1, n, m->tmp);
     715          if (k != n) {
     716                  log_error("Failed to read from file: %s", STRERROR_OR_EOF(errno));
     717                  return MHD_CONTENT_READER_END_WITH_ERROR;
     718          }
     719  
     720          return (ssize_t) k;
     721  }
     722  
     723  static int request_handler_fields(
     724                  struct MHD_Connection *connection,
     725                  const char *field,
     726                  void *connection_cls) {
     727  
     728          _cleanup_(MHD_destroy_responsep) struct MHD_Response *response = NULL;
     729          RequestMeta *m = ASSERT_PTR(connection_cls);
     730          int r;
     731  
     732          assert(connection);
     733  
     734          r = open_journal(m);
     735          if (r < 0)
     736                  return mhd_respondf(connection, r, MHD_HTTP_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "Failed to open journal: %m");
     737  
     738          if (request_parse_accept(m, connection) < 0)
     739                  return mhd_respond(connection, MHD_HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, "Failed to parse Accept header.");
     740  
     741          r = sd_journal_query_unique(m->journal, field);
     742          if (r < 0)
     743                  return mhd_respond(connection, MHD_HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, "Failed to query unique fields.");
     744  
     745          response = MHD_create_response_from_callback(MHD_SIZE_UNKNOWN, 4*1024, request_reader_fields, m, NULL);
     746          if (!response)
     747                  return respond_oom(connection);
     748  
     749          if (MHD_add_response_header(response, "Content-Type", mime_types[m->mode == OUTPUT_JSON ? OUTPUT_JSON : OUTPUT_SHORT]) == MHD_NO)
     750                  return respond_oom(connection);
     751  
     752          return MHD_queue_response(connection, MHD_HTTP_OK, response);
     753  }

     755  static int request_handler_redirect(
     756                  struct MHD_Connection *connection,
     757                  const char *target) {
     758  
     759          _cleanup_free_ char *page = NULL;

     761

     766                  return respond_oom(connection);

     774              MHD_add_response_header(response, "Location", target) == MHD_NO)

     777          return MHD_queue_response(connection, MHD_HTTP_MOVED_PERMANENTLY, response);

     780  static int request_handler_file(
     781                  struct MHD_Connection *connection,
     782                  const char *path,
     783                  const char *mime_type) {
     784  
     785          _cleanup_(MHD_destroy_responsep) struct MHD_Response *response = NULL;
     786          _cleanup_close_ int fd = -EBADF;

     788

     793          fd = open(path, O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC);
     794          if (fd < 0)
     795                  return mhd_respondf(connection, errno, MHD_HTTP_NOT_FOUND, "Failed to open file %s: %m", path);
     796  
     797          if (fstat(fd, &st) < 0)
     798                  return mhd_respondf(connection, errno, MHD_HTTP_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "Failed to stat file: %m");
     799  
     800          response = MHD_create_response_from_fd_at_offset64(st.st_size, fd, 0);

     803          TAKE_FD(fd);
     804  
     805          if (MHD_add_response_header(response, "Content-Type", mime_type) == MHD_NO)
     806                  return respond_oom(connection);
     807  
     808          return MHD_queue_response(connection, MHD_HTTP_OK, response);
     809  }

     811  static int get_virtualization(char **v) {
     812          _cleanup_(sd_bus_unrefp) sd_bus *bus = NULL;
     813          char *b = NULL;
     814          int r;
     815  
     816          r = sd_bus_default_system(&bus);
     817          if (r < 0)
     818                  return r;
     819  
     820          r = bus_get_property_string(bus, bus_systemd_mgr, "Virtualization", NULL, &b);
     821          if (r < 0)
     822                  return r;
     823  
     824          if (isempty(b)) {
     825                  free(b);
     826                  *v = NULL;

     829

     831          return 1;
