      99  static int skip_ok_port_res(int fd, const char *path, const char *port) {
     100          struct timeval oldtv;
     101          socklen_t oldtv_size = sizeof(oldtv);
     102          if (getsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVTIMEO, &oldtv, &oldtv_size) < 0)
     103                  return log_error_errno(errno, "Failed to get socket receive timeout for %s: %m", path);
     104          if (oldtv_size != sizeof(oldtv))
     105                  return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EIO), "Unexpected size of socket receive timeout for %s", path);
     106          if (setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVTIMEO, TIMEVAL_STORE(HEADER_READ_TIMEOUT_USEC), sizeof(struct timeval)) < 0)
     107                  return log_error_errno(errno, "Failed to set socket receive timeout for %s: %m", path);
     108  
     109          char recv_buf[STRLEN("OK 65535\n")];
     110          size_t bytes_recv = 0, bytes_avail = 0, pos = 0;
     111          static const char expected_prefix[] = "OK ";
     112  
     113          for (;;) {
     114                  if (pos >= bytes_avail) {
     115                          assert(bytes_recv <= bytes_avail);
     116                          if (bytes_avail >= sizeof(recv_buf)) {
     117                                  /*
     118                                    Full buffer means that we have peeked as many bytes as possible and not seeing the ending \n .
     119                                    So the server is believed to not send OK PORT response, and we just pass out the socket to ssh client,
     120                                    and let it handle the connection.
     121  
     122                                    If we have not received any bytes from the socket buffer, we can safely pass out the socket,
     123                                    since no change has been made to the socket buffer. Otherwise, if some bytes have been received,
     124                                    the socket buffer has been changed, the only option is to give up and terminate the connection.
     125                                    Similar logic applies below when we meet other kinds of unexpected responses.
     126                                  */
     127                                  if (bytes_recv == 0) {
     128                                          log_debug("Received too many bytes while waiting for OK PORT response from %s\n"
     129                                                    "Assume the multiplexer is not sending OK PORT.",
     130                                                    path);
     131                                          goto passout_fd;
     132                                  }
     133                                  return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EIO), "Received too many bytes while waiting for OK PORT response from %s", path);
     134                          }
     135                          if (bytes_avail > bytes_recv) {
     136                                  /*
     137                                    Discard already peeked bytes before peeking more.
     138  
     139                                    XXX: We cannot use SO_RCVLOWAT to set the minimum number of bytes to be peeked to peek entire
     140                                         OK PORT response at once to prevent changes to the recving buffer, because SO_RCVLOWAT
     141                                         does not work on unix sockets with recv(..., MSG_PEEK). Also poll() does not help here,
     142                                         because poll() returns readable as long as there is any data in the socket buffer for
     143                                         unix sockets, not respecting SO_RCVLOWAT.
     144  
     145                                    XXX: We could have used SO_PEEK_OFF to continuously peek more data without changing the socket
     146                                         receive buffer, but this function breaks since Linux 4.3 due to a kernel bug, which is fixed
     147                                         in Linux 6.18 commit 7bf3a476ce43 ("af_unix: Read sk_peek_offset() again after sleeping in
     148                                         unix_stream_read_generic()."). It is also not possible to detect whether the kernel is
     149                                         affected by this bug at runtime.
     150  
     151                                    As a result, we have no other choice but to discard already peeked data here.
     152                                  */
     153                                  ssize_t rlen = recv(fd, recv_buf + bytes_recv, bytes_avail - bytes_recv, /* flags= */ 0);
     154                                  if (rlen < 0)
     155                                          return log_error_errno(errno, "Failed to discard OK PORT response from %s: %m", path);
     156                                  if ((size_t) rlen != bytes_avail - bytes_recv)
     157                                          return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EIO), "Short read while discarding OK PORT response from %s", path);
     158                                  log_debug("Successfully discarded %zi bytes of response: %.*s", rlen, (int) rlen, recv_buf + bytes_recv);
     159                                  bytes_recv = bytes_avail;
     160                          }
     161                          ssize_t len = recv(fd, recv_buf + bytes_avail, sizeof(recv_buf) - bytes_avail, MSG_PEEK);
     162                          if (len < 0) {
     163                                  if (errno != EAGAIN)
     164                                          return log_error_errno(errno, "Failed to receive OK from %s: %m", path);
     165                                  if (bytes_recv == 0) {
     166                                          log_debug("Timeout while waiting for OK PORT response from %s\n"
     167                                                    "Assume the multiplexer will not send OK PORT.",
     168                                                    path);
     169                                          goto passout_fd;
     170                                  }
     171                                  return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EIO), "Timed out to receive OK PORT from %s", path);
     172  
     173                          }
     174                          if (len == 0) {
     175                                  log_debug("Connection closed while waiting for OK PORT response from %s", path);
     176                                  if (bytes_recv == 0) {
     177                                          log_debug("No data received, which means the connecting port is not open.");
     178                                          return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(ECONNREFUSED), "Port %s on %s is not open", port, path);
     179                                  }
     180                                  return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EIO), "Connection closed before full OK PORT response received from %s.", path);
     181                          }
     182                          bytes_avail += len;
     183                  }
     184                  assert(pos < bytes_avail);
     185                  if (pos < strlen(expected_prefix) && recv_buf[pos] != expected_prefix[pos]) {
     186                          if (bytes_recv == 0) {
     187                                  log_debug("Received response does not start with expected OK PORT response from %s\n"
     188                                            "Assume the multiplexer will not send OK PORT.",
     189                                            path);
     190                                  goto passout_fd;
     191                          }
     192                          return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EIO), "Received invalid response while waiting for OK PORT from %s", path);
     193                  }
     194                  if (recv_buf[pos] == '\n') {
     195                          pos += 1;
     196                          break;
     197                  }
     198                  pos += 1;
     199          }
     200  
     201          assert(pos <= sizeof(recv_buf));
     202          assert(bytes_recv <= pos);
     203          if (bytes_recv < pos) {
     204                  ssize_t len = recv(fd, recv_buf + bytes_recv, pos - bytes_recv, /* flags= */ 0);
     205                  if (len < 0)
     206                          return log_error_errno(errno, "Failed to discard OK PORT response from %s: %m", path);
     207                  if ((size_t) len != pos - bytes_recv)
     208                          return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EIO), "Short read while discarding OK PORT response from %s", path);
     209                  log_debug("Successfully discarded response from %s: %.*s", path, (int) pos, recv_buf);
     210          }
     211  
     212  passout_fd:
     213          if (setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVTIMEO, &oldtv, sizeof(oldtv)) < 0)
     214                  return log_error_errno(errno, "Failed to restore socket receive timeout for %s: %m", path);
     215          return 0;
     216  }

     218  static int process_vsock_mux(const char *path, const char *port) {
     219          int r;
     220  
     221          assert(path);
     222          assert(port);
     223  
     224          /* We assume the path is absolute unless it starts with a dot (or is already explicitly absolute) */
     225          _cleanup_free_ char *prefixed = NULL;
     226          if (!STARTSWITH_SET(path, "/", "./")) {
     227                  prefixed = strjoin("/", path);
     228                  if (!prefixed)
     229                          return log_oom();
     230  
     231                  path = prefixed;
     232          }
     233  
     234          _cleanup_close_ int fd = socket(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM|SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0);
     235          if (fd < 0)
     236                  return log_error_errno(errno, "Failed to allocate AF_UNIX socket: %m");
     237  
     238          r = connect_unix_path(fd, AT_FDCWD, path);
     239          if (r < 0)
     240                  return log_error_errno(r, "Failed to connect to AF_UNIX socket %s: %m", path);
     241  
     242          /* Based on the protocol as defined here:
     243           * https://github.com/cloud-hypervisor/cloud-hypervisor/blob/main/docs/vsock.md
     244           * https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/main/docs/vsock.md */
     245          _cleanup_free_ char *connect_cmd = NULL;
     246          connect_cmd = strjoin("CONNECT ", port, "\n");
     247          if (!connect_cmd)
     248                  return log_oom();
     249  
     250          r = loop_write(fd, connect_cmd, SIZE_MAX);
     251          if (r < 0)
     252                  return log_error_errno(r, "Failed to send CONNECT to %s:%s: %m", path, port);
     253  
     254          r = skip_ok_port_res(fd, path, port);
     255          if (r < 0)
     256                  return r;
     257  
     258          r = send_one_fd_iov(STDOUT_FILENO, fd, &iovec_nul_byte, /* iovlen= */ 1, /* flags= */ 0);
     259          if (r < 0)
     260                  return log_error_errno(r, "Failed to send socket via STDOUT: %m");
     261  
     262          log_debug("Successfully sent AF_UNIX socket via STDOUT.");
     263          return 0;
     264  }

     333                  { "class",    SD_JSON_VARIANT_STRING,   sd_json_dispatch_const_string, voffsetof(p, class),   SD_JSON_MANDATORY },
     334                  { "service",  SD_JSON_VARIANT_STRING,   sd_json_dispatch_const_string, voffsetof(p, service), 0                 },

     343  
     344                  if (!streq_ptr(p.service, "systemd-nspawn"))
     345                          return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EMEDIUMTYPE), "Don't know how to SSH into '%s' container %s.", p.service, machine);
     346  
     347                  r = runtime_directory_generic(scope, "systemd/nspawn/unix-export", &path);
     348                  if (r < 0)
     349                          return log_error_errno(r, "Failed to determine runtime directory: %m");
     350  
     351                  if (!path_extend(&path, machine, "ssh"))
     352                          return log_oom();
     353  
     354                  r = is_socket(path);
     355                  if (r < 0)
     356                          return log_error_errno(r, "Failed to check if '%s' exists and is a socket: %m", path);
     357                  if (r == 0)
     358                          return log_error_errno(
     359                                          SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(ENOENT),
     360                                          "'%s' does not exist or is not a socket, are sshd and systemd-ssh-generator installed and enabled in the container?",
     361                                          path);

     363                  return process_unix(path);
     364          }
     365  
     366          if (!streq(p.class, "vm"))
     367                  return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EMEDIUMTYPE), "Don't know how to SSH into machine %s with class '%s'.", machine, p.class);
     368  
     369          if (p.cid == VMADDR_CID_ANY)
     370                  return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EINVAL), "Machine %s has no AF_VSOCK CID assigned.", machine);
     371  
     372          return process_vsock_cid(p.cid, port);
     373  }

     375  static char *startswith_sep(const char *s, const char *prefix) {
     376          const char *p = startswith(s, prefix);
     377  
     378          if (p && IN_SET(*p, '/', '%'))
     379                  return (char*) p + 1;
     380  
     381          return NULL;
     382  }

     384  static int run(int argc, char* argv[]) {
     385  
     386          log_setup();
     387  
     388          if (argc != 3)
     389                  return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EINVAL), "Expected two arguments: host and port.");
     390  
     391          const char *host = argv[1], *port = argv[2];
     392  
     393          const char *p = startswith_sep(host, "vsock");
     394          if (p)
     395                  return process_vsock_string(p, port);
     396  
     397          p = startswith_sep(host, "unix");
     398          if (p)
     399                  return process_unix(p);
     400  
     401          p = startswith_sep(host, "vsock-mux");
     402          if (p)
     403                  return process_vsock_mux(p, port);
     404  
     405          p = startswith_sep(host, "machine");
     406          if (p)
     407                  return process_machine(p, port);
     408  
     409          return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EINVAL), "Don't know how to parse host name specification: %s", host);
     410  }

     375  static char *startswith_sep(const char *s, const char *prefix) {
     376          const char *p = startswith(s, prefix);
     377  
     378          if (p && IN_SET(*p, '/', '%'))
     379                  return (char*) p + 1;
     380  
     381          return NULL;
     382  }

     384  static int run(int argc, char* argv[]) {
     385  
     386          log_setup();
     387  
     388          if (argc != 3)
     389                  return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EINVAL), "Expected two arguments: host and port.");
     390  
     391          const char *host = argv[1], *port = argv[2];
     392  
     393          const char *p = startswith_sep(host, "vsock");
     394          if (p)
     395                  return process_vsock_string(p, port);
     396  
     397          p = startswith_sep(host, "unix");
     398          if (p)
     399                  return process_unix(p);
     400  
     401          p = startswith_sep(host, "vsock-mux");
     402          if (p)
     403                  return process_vsock_mux(p, port);
     404  
     405          p = startswith_sep(host, "machine");
     406          if (p)
     407                  return process_machine(p, port);
     408  
     409          return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EINVAL), "Don't know how to parse host name specification: %s", host);
     410  }
     411  
     412  DEFINE_MAIN_FUNCTION(run);

     375  static char *startswith_sep(const char *s, const char *prefix) {
     376          const char *p = startswith(s, prefix);
     377  
     378          if (p && IN_SET(*p, '/', '%'))
     379                  return (char*) p + 1;
     380  
     381          return NULL;
     382  }

     384  static int run(int argc, char* argv[]) {
     385  
     386          log_setup();
     387  
     388          if (argc != 3)
     389                  return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EINVAL), "Expected two arguments: host and port.");
     390  
     391          const char *host = argv[1], *port = argv[2];
     392  
     393          const char *p = startswith_sep(host, "vsock");
     394          if (p)
     395                  return process_vsock_string(p, port);
     396  
     397          p = startswith_sep(host, "unix");
     398          if (p)
     399                  return process_unix(p);
     400  
     401          p = startswith_sep(host, "vsock-mux");
     402          if (p)
     403                  return process_vsock_mux(p, port);
     404  
     405          p = startswith_sep(host, "machine");
     406          if (p)
     407                  return process_machine(p, port);
     408  
     409          return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EINVAL), "Don't know how to parse host name specification: %s", host);
     410  }

     387  
     388          if (argc != 3)
     389                  return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EINVAL), "Expected two arguments: host and port.");
     390  
     391          const char *host = argv[1], *port = argv[2];
     392  
     393          const char *p = startswith_sep(host, "vsock");
     394          if (p)
     395                  return process_vsock_string(p, port);
     396  
     397          p = startswith_sep(host, "unix");
     398          if (p)

     400  
     401          p = startswith_sep(host, "vsock-mux");
     402          if (p)
     403                  return process_vsock_mux(p, port);
     404  
     405          p = startswith_sep(host, "machine");
     406          if (p)
     407                  return process_machine(p, port);
     408  
     409          return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EINVAL), "Don't know how to parse host name specification: %s", host);
     410  }

     375  static char *startswith_sep(const char *s, const char *prefix) {
     376          const char *p = startswith(s, prefix);
     377  
     378          if (p && IN_SET(*p, '/', '%'))
     379                  return (char*) p + 1;
     380  
     381          return NULL;
     382  }

     384  static int run(int argc, char* argv[]) {
     385  
     386          log_setup();
     387  
     388          if (argc != 3)
     389                  return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EINVAL), "Expected two arguments: host and port.");
     390  
     391          const char *host = argv[1], *port = argv[2];
     392  
     393          const char *p = startswith_sep(host, "vsock");
     394          if (p)
     395                  return process_vsock_string(p, port);
     396  
     397          p = startswith_sep(host, "unix");
     398          if (p)
     399                  return process_unix(p);
     400  
     401          p = startswith_sep(host, "vsock-mux");
     402          if (p)
     403                  return process_vsock_mux(p, port);
     404  
     405          p = startswith_sep(host, "machine");
     406          if (p)
     407                  return process_machine(p, port);
     408  
     409          return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EINVAL), "Don't know how to parse host name specification: %s", host);
     410  }

      23  static int process_vsock_cid(unsigned cid, const char *port) {
      24          int r;
      25  
      26          assert(cid != VMADDR_CID_ANY);
      27          assert(port);
      28  
      29          union sockaddr_union sa = {
      30                  .vm.svm_cid = cid,
      31                  .vm.svm_family = AF_VSOCK,
      32          };
      33  
      34          r = vsock_parse_port(port, &sa.vm.svm_port);
      35          if (r < 0)
      36                  return log_error_errno(r, "Failed to parse vsock port: %s", port);
      37  
      38          _cleanup_close_ int fd = socket(AF_VSOCK, SOCK_STREAM|SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0);
      39          if (fd < 0)
      40                  return log_error_errno(errno, "Failed to allocate AF_VSOCK socket: %m");
      41  
      42          if (connect(fd, &sa.sa, sockaddr_len(&sa)) < 0)
      43                  return log_error_errno(errno, "Failed to connect to vsock:%u:%u: %m", sa.vm.svm_cid, sa.vm.svm_port);
      44  
      45          /* OpenSSH wants us to send a single byte along with the file descriptor, hence do so */
      46          r = send_one_fd_iov(STDOUT_FILENO, fd, &iovec_nul_byte, /* iovlen= */ 1, /* flags= */ 0);
      47          if (r < 0)
      48                  return log_error_errno(r, "Failed to send socket via STDOUT: %m");
      49  
      50          log_debug("Successfully sent AF_VSOCK socket via STDOUT.");
      51          return 0;
      52  }

     218  static int process_vsock_mux(const char *path, const char *port) {

     220  
     221          assert(path);

     229                          return log_oom();
     230

     235          if (fd < 0)
     236                  return log_error_errno(errno, "Failed to allocate AF_UNIX socket: %m");
     237  
     238          r = connect_unix_path(fd, AT_FDCWD, path);
     239          if (r < 0)
     240                  return log_error_errno(r, "Failed to connect to AF_UNIX socket %s: %m", path);
     241  
     242          /* Based on the protocol as defined here:
     243           * https://github.com/cloud-hypervisor/cloud-hypervisor/blob/main/docs/vsock.md
     244           * https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/main/docs/vsock.md */

     253  
     254          r = skip_ok_port_res(fd, path, port);

     257  
     258          r = send_one_fd_iov(STDOUT_FILENO, fd, &iovec_nul_byte, /* iovlen= */ 1, /* flags= */ 0);
     259          if (r < 0)
     260                  return log_error_errno(r, "Failed to send socket via STDOUT: %m");

     262          log_debug("Successfully sent AF_UNIX socket via STDOUT.");

     375  static char *startswith_sep(const char *s, const char *prefix) {
     376          const char *p = startswith(s, prefix);

     379                  return (char*) p + 1;
     380

     384  static int run(int argc, char* argv[]) {
     385  
     386          log_setup();
     387  
     388          if (argc != 3)
     389                  return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EINVAL), "Expected two arguments: host and port.");
     390  
     391          const char *host = argv[1], *port = argv[2];
     392  
     393          const char *p = startswith_sep(host, "vsock");
     394          if (p)
     395                  return process_vsock_string(p, port);
     396  
     397          p = startswith_sep(host, "unix");
     398          if (p)
     399                  return process_unix(p);
     400  
     401          p = startswith_sep(host, "vsock-mux");
     402          if (p)
     403                  return process_vsock_mux(p, port);
     404  
     405          p = startswith_sep(host, "machine");
     406          if (p)
     407                  return process_machine(p, port);
     408  
     409          return log_error_errno(SYNTHETIC_ERRNO(EINVAL), "Don't know how to parse host name specification: %s", host);
     410  }

     412  DEFINE_MAIN_FUNCTION(run);

      93  def guess_efi_arch() -> str:
      94      arch = os.uname().machine
      95  
      96      for glob, mapping in EFI_ARCH_MAP.items():
      97          if fnmatch.fnmatch(arch, glob):
      98              efi_arch, *fallback = mapping
      99              break
     100      else:
     101          raise ValueError(f'Unsupported architecture {arch}')
     102  
     103      # This makes sense only on some architectures, but it also probably doesn't
     104      # hurt on others, so let's just apply the check everywhere.
     105      if fallback:
     106          fw_platform_size = Path('/sys/firmware/efi/fw_platform_size')
     107          try:
     108              size = fw_platform_size.read_text().strip()
     109          except FileNotFoundError:
     110              pass
     111          else:
     112              if int(size) == 32:
     113                  efi_arch = fallback[0]
     114  
     115      # print(f'Host arch {arch!r}, EFI arch {efi_arch!r}')
     116      return efi_arch

     144  def read_env_file(text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
     145      result = {}
     146  
     147      for line in text.splitlines():
     148          line = line.rstrip()
     149          if not line or line.startswith('#'):
     150              continue
     151          if m := re.match(r'([A-Z][A-Z_0-9]+)=(.*)', line):
     152              name, val = m.groups()
     153              if val and val[0] in '"\'':
     154                  val = next(shlex.shlex(val, posix=True))
     155  
     156              result[name] = val
     157          else:
     158              print(f'bad line {line!r}', file=sys.stderr)
     159  
     160      return result

     163  def get_zboot_kernel(f: IO[bytes]) -> bytes:
     164      """Decompress zboot efistub kernel if compressed. Return contents."""
     165      # See linux/drivers/firmware/efi/libstub/Makefile.zboot
     166      # and linux/drivers/firmware/efi/libstub/zboot-header.S
     167  
     168      # 4 bytes at offset 0x08 contain the starting offset of compressed data
     169      f.seek(8)
     170      _start = f.read(4)
     171      start = struct.unpack('<i', _start)[0]
     172  
     173      # Reading 4 bytes from address 0x0c is the size of compressed data,
     174      # but it needs to be corrected according to the compressed type.
     175      f.seek(0xC)
     176      _sizes = f.read(4)
     177      size = struct.unpack('<i', _sizes)[0]
     178  
     179      # Read 6 bytes from address 0x18, which is a nul-terminated
     180      # string representing the compressed type.
     181      f.seek(0x18)
     182      comp_type = f.read(6)
     183      f.seek(start)
     184      if comp_type.startswith(b'gzip'):
     185          gzip = try_import('gzip')
     186          data = f.read(size)
     187          return cast(bytes, gzip.decompress(data))
     188      elif comp_type.startswith(b'lz4'):
     189          lz4 = try_import('lz4.frame', 'lz4')
     190          data = f.read(size)
     191          return cast(bytes, lz4.frame.decompress(data))
     192      elif comp_type.startswith(b'lzma'):
     193          lzma = try_import('lzma')
     194          data = f.read(size)
     195          return cast(bytes, lzma.decompress(data))
     196      elif comp_type.startswith(b'lzo'):
     197          raise NotImplementedError('lzo decompression not implemented')
     198      elif comp_type.startswith(b'xzkern'):
     199          raise NotImplementedError('xzkern decompression not implemented')
     200      elif comp_type.startswith(b'zstd'):
     201          try:
     202              zstd = try_import('compression.zstd')
     203              data = f.read(size)
     204              return cast(bytes, zstd.zstd.ZstdDecompressor().decompress(data))
     205          except ValueError:
     206              zstd = try_import('zstandard')
     207              data = f.read(size)
     208              return cast(bytes, zstd.ZstdDecompressor().stream_reader(data).read())
     209  
     210      raise NotImplementedError(f'unknown compressed type: {comp_type!r}')

     213  def maybe_decompress(filename: Union[str, Path]) -> bytes:
     214      """Decompress file if compressed. Return contents."""
     215      f = open(filename, 'rb')
     216      start = f.read(4)
     217      f.seek(0)
     218  
     219      if start.startswith(b'\x7fELF'):
     220          # not compressed
     221          return f.read()
     222  
     223      if start.startswith(b'MZ'):
     224          f.seek(4)
     225          img_type = f.read(4)
     226          if img_type.startswith(b'zimg'):
     227              # zboot efistub kernel
     228              return get_zboot_kernel(f)
     229          else:
     230              # not compressed aarch64 and riscv64
     231              return f.read()
     232  
     233      if start.startswith(b'\x1f\x8b'):
     234          gzip = try_import('gzip')
     235          return cast(bytes, gzip.open(f).read())
     236  
     237      if start.startswith(b'\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd'):
     238          try:
     239              zstd = try_import('compression.zstd')
     240              return cast(bytes, zstd.zstd.ZstdDecompressor().decompress(f.read()))
     241          except ValueError:
     242              zstd = try_import('zstandard')
     243              return cast(bytes, zstd.ZstdDecompressor().stream_reader(f.read()).read())
     244  
     245      if start.startswith(b'\x02\x21\x4c\x18'):
     246          lz4 = try_import('lz4.frame', 'lz4')
     247          return cast(bytes, lz4.frame.decompress(f.read()))
     248  
     249      if start.startswith(b'\x04\x22\x4d\x18'):
     250          print('Newer lz4 stream format detected! This may not boot!', file=sys.stderr)
     251          lz4 = try_import('lz4.frame', 'lz4')
     252          return cast(bytes, lz4.frame.decompress(f.read()))
     253  
     254      if start.startswith(b'\x89LZO'):
     255          # python3-lzo is not packaged for Fedora
     256          raise NotImplementedError('lzo decompression not implemented')
     257  
     258      if start.startswith(b'BZh'):
     259          bz2 = try_import('bz2', 'bzip2')
     260          return cast(bytes, bz2.open(f).read())
     261  
     262      if start.startswith(b'\x5d\x00\x00'):
     263          lzma = try_import('lzma')
     264          return cast(bytes, lzma.open(f).read())
     265  
     266      raise NotImplementedError(f'unknown file format (starts with {start!r})')

     326      VERSION_PATTERN = r'(?P<version>[a-z0-9._+-]+) \([^ )]+\) (?:#.*)'
     327  
     328      NOTES_PATTERN = r'^\s+Linux\s+0x[0-9a-f]+\s+OPEN\n\s+description data: (?P<version>[0-9a-f ]+)\s*$'
     329  
     330      # Linux version 6.0.8-300.fc37.ppc64le (mockbuild@buildvm-ppc64le-03.iad2.fedoraproject.org)
     331      # (gcc (GCC) 12.2.1 20220819 (Red Hat 12.2.1-2), GNU ld version 2.38-24.fc37)

     333      TEXT_PATTERN = rb'Linux version (?P<version>\d\.\S+) \('

     335      @classmethod
     336      def scrape_x86(cls, filename: Path, opts: Optional[UkifyConfig] = None) -> str:
     337          # Based on https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/mkinitcpio/mkinitcpio/-/blob/master/functions#L136
     338          # and https://docs.kernel.org/arch/x86/boot.html#the-real-mode-kernel-header
     339          with open(filename, 'rb') as f:
     340              f.seek(0x202)
     341              magic = f.read(4)
     342              if magic != b'HdrS':
     343                  raise ValueError('Real-Mode Kernel Header magic not found')
     344              f.seek(0x20E)
     345              offset = f.read(1)[0] + f.read(1)[0] * 256  # Pointer to kernel version string
     346              f.seek(0x200 + offset)
     347              text = f.read(128)
     348          text = text.split(b'\0', maxsplit=1)[0]
     349          decoded = text.decode()
     350  
     351          if not (m := re.match(cls.VERSION_PATTERN, decoded)):
     352              raise ValueError(f'Cannot parse version-host-release uname string: {text!r}')
     353          return m.group('version')
     354  
     355      @classmethod
     356      def scrape_elf(cls, filename: Path, opts: Optional[UkifyConfig] = None) -> str:
     357          readelf = find_tool('readelf', opts=opts)
     358  
     359          cmd = [
     360              readelf,
     361              '--notes',
     362              filename,
     363          ]
     364  
     365          print('+', shell_join(cmd), file=sys.stderr)
     366          try:
     367              notes = subprocess.check_output(cmd, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
     368          except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
     369              raise ValueError(e.stderr.strip()) from e
     370  
     371          if not (m := re.search(cls.NOTES_PATTERN, notes, re.MULTILINE)):
     372              raise ValueError('Cannot find Linux version note')
     373  
     374          text = ''.join(chr(int(c, 16)) for c in m.group('version').split())
     375          return text.rstrip('\0')
     376  
     377      @classmethod
     378      def scrape_generic(cls, filename: Path, opts: Optional[UkifyConfig] = None) -> str:

     382  
     383          # Based on https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/mkinitcpio/mkinitcpio/-/blob/master/functions#L209

     385          text = maybe_decompress(filename)
     386          if not (m := re.search(cls.TEXT_PATTERN, text)):
     387              raise ValueError(f'Cannot find {cls.TEXT_PATTERN!r} in {filename}')

     391      @classmethod

     423  @dataclasses.dataclass
     424  class Section:
     425      name: str
     426      content: Optional[Path]
     427      tmpfile: Optional[IO[Any]] = None
     428      measure: bool = False
     429      output_mode: Optional[str] = None
     430  
     431      @classmethod
     432      def create(cls, name: str, contents: Union[str, bytes, Path, None], **kwargs: Any) -> 'Section':
     433          if isinstance(contents, (str, bytes)):
     434              mode = 'wt' if isinstance(contents, str) else 'wb'
     435              tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode=mode, prefix=f'tmp{name}')
     436              tmp.write(contents)
     437              tmp.flush()
     438              contents = Path(tmp.name)
     439          else:
     440              tmp = None
     441  
     442          return cls(name, contents, tmpfile=tmp, **kwargs)
     443  
     444      @classmethod
     445      def parse_input(cls, s: str) -> 'Section':
     446          try:
     447              name, contents, *rest = s.split(':')
     448          except ValueError as e:
     449              raise ValueError(f'Cannot parse section spec (name or contents missing): {s!r}') from e
     450          if rest:
     451              raise ValueError(f'Cannot parse section spec (extraneous parameters): {s!r}')
     452  
     453          if contents.startswith('@'):
     454              sec = cls.create(name, Path(contents[1:]))
     455          else:
     456              sec = cls.create(name, contents)
     457  
     458          sec.check_name()
     459          return sec
     460  
     461      @classmethod
     462      def parse_output(cls, s: str) -> 'Section':
     463          if not (m := re.match(r'([a-zA-Z0-9_.]+):(text|binary)(?:@(.+))?', s)):
     464              raise ValueError(f'Cannot parse section spec: {s!r}')
     465  
     466          name, ttype, out = m.groups()
     467          out = Path(out) if out else None
     468  
     469          return cls.create(name, out, output_mode=ttype)
     470  
     471      def check_name(self) -> None:
     472          # PE section names with more than 8 characters are legal, but our stub does
     473          # not support them.
     474          if not self.name.isascii() or not self.name.isprintable():
     475              raise ValueError(f'Bad section name: {self.name!r}')
     476          if len(self.name) > 8:
     477              raise ValueError(f'Section name too long: {self.name!r}')

     484  
     485      def add_section(self, section: Section) -> None:
     486          start = 0
     487  
     488          # Start search at last .profile section, if there is one
     489          for i, s in enumerate(self.sections):
     490              if s.name == '.profile':
     491                  start = i + 1
     492  
     493          multiple_allowed_sections = ['.dtbauto', '.efifw']
     494          if any(
     495              section.name == s.name for s in self.sections[start:] if s.name not in multiple_allowed_sections
     496          ):
     497              raise ValueError(f'Duplicate section {section.name}')
     498  
     499          self.sections += [section]

     520              raise ValueError(f'Invalid sign tool: {name!r}')
     521

     523  class PeSign(SignTool):
     524      @staticmethod
     525      def sign(input_f: str, output_f: str, opts: UkifyConfig) -> None:
     526          assert opts.sb_certdir is not None
     527          assert opts.sb_cert_name is not None
     528  
     529          tool = find_tool('pesign', opts=opts, msg='pesign, required for signing, is not installed')
     530          cmd = [
     531              tool,
     532              '-s',
     533              '--force',
     534              '-n', opts.sb_certdir,
     535              '-c', opts.sb_cert_name,
     536              '-i', input_f,
     537              '-o', output_f,
     538          ]  # fmt: skip
     539  
     540          print('+', shell_join(cmd), file=sys.stderr)
     541          subprocess.check_call(cmd)
     542  
     543      @staticmethod
     544      def verify(input_f: Path, opts: UkifyConfig) -> bool:
     545          assert input_f is not None
     546  
     547          tool = find_tool('pesign', opts=opts)
     548          cmd = [tool, '-i', input_f, '-S']
     549  
     550          print('+', shell_join(cmd), file=sys.stderr)
     551          info = subprocess.check_output(cmd, text=True)
     552  
     553          return 'No signatures found.' in info

     591          assert opts.sb_key is not None

     607                  if opts.signing_engine is not None

     609              ),

     612                  if opts.signing_provider is not None

     617                  if opts.certificate_provider is not None
     618                  else []
     619              ),
     620              input_f,
     621              '--output', output_f,

     633      banks = re.split(r',|\s+', s)

     638  KNOWN_PHASES = (
     639      'enter-initrd',
     640      'leave-initrd',
     641      'sysinit',
     642      'ready',
     643      'shutdown',
     644      'final',
     645  )

     647  
     648  def parse_phase_paths(s: str) -> list[str]:
     649      # Split on commas or whitespace here. Commas might be hard to parse visually.
     650      paths = re.split(r',|\s+', s)
     651  
     652      for path in paths:
     653          for phase in path.split(':'):
     654              if phase not in KNOWN_PHASES:
     655                  raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f'Unknown boot phase {phase!r} ({path=})')
     656  
     657      return paths

     660  def check_splash(filename: Optional[Path]) -> None:
     661      if filename is None:
     662          return
     663  
     664      # import is delayed, to avoid import when the splash image is not used
     665      try:
     666          from PIL import Image
     667      except ImportError:
     668          return
     669  
     670      img = Image.open(filename, formats=['BMP'])
     671      print(f'Splash image {filename} is {img.width}×{img.height} pixels', file=sys.stderr)
     672  
     673  
     674  def check_inputs(opts: UkifyConfig) -> None:
     675      for name, value in vars(opts).items():
     676          if name in {'output', 'tools'}:
     677              continue
     678  
     679          if isinstance(value, Path):
     680              # Check that we can open the directory or file, or generate and exception
     681              if value.is_dir():
     682                  value.iterdir()
     683              else:
     684                  value.open().close()
     685          elif isinstance(value, list):
     686              for item in value:
     687                  if isinstance(item, Path):
     688                      if item.is_dir():
     689                          item.iterdir()
     690                      else:
     691                          item.open().close()
     692  
     693      check_splash(opts.splash)

     696  def check_cert_and_keys_nonexistent(opts: UkifyConfig) -> None:
     697      # Raise if any of the keys and certs are found on disk
     698      paths: Iterator[Union[str, Path, None]] = itertools.chain(
     699          (opts.sb_key, opts.sb_cert),
     700          *((priv_key, pub_key, cert) for priv_key, pub_key, cert, _ in key_path_groups(opts)),
     701      )
     702      for path in paths:
     703          if path and Path(path).exists():
     704              raise ValueError(f'{path} is present')
