     706  
     707  def find_tool(
     708      name: str,
     709      fallback: Optional[str] = None,
     710      opts: Optional[UkifyConfig] = None,
     711      msg: str = 'Tool {name} not installed!',
     712  ) -> Union[str, Path]:
     713      if opts and opts.tools:
     714          for d in opts.tools:
     715              tool = d / name
     716              if tool.exists():
     717                  return tool
     718  
     719      if shutil.which(name) is not None:
     720          return name
     721  
     722      if fallback is None:
     723          raise ValueError(msg.format(name=name))
     724  
     725      return fallback
     726  
     727  
     728  def combine_signatures(pcrsigs: list[dict[str, str]]) -> str:
     729      combined: collections.defaultdict[str, list[str]] = collections.defaultdict(list)
     730      for pcrsig in pcrsigs:
     731          for bank, sigs in pcrsig.items():
     732              for sig in sigs:
     733                  if sig not in combined[bank]:
     734                      combined[bank] += [sig]
     735      return json.dumps(combined)
     736  
     737  
     738  def key_path_groups(opts: UkifyConfig) -> Iterator[tuple[str, Optional[str], Optional[str], Optional[str]]]:
     739      if not opts.pcr_private_keys:
     740          return
     741  
     742      n_priv = len(opts.pcr_private_keys)
     743      pub_keys = opts.pcr_public_keys or []
     744      certs = opts.pcr_certificates or []
     745      pp_groups = opts.phase_path_groups or []
     746  
     747      yield from itertools.zip_longest(
     748          opts.pcr_private_keys,
     749          pub_keys[:n_priv],
     750          certs[:n_priv],
     751          pp_groups[:n_priv],
     752          fillvalue=None,
     753      )
     754  
     755  
     756  def pe_strip_section_name(name: bytes) -> str:
     757      return name.rstrip(b'\x00').decode()
     758  
     759  
     760  def pe_section_size(section: pefile.SectionStructure) -> int:
     761      return cast(int, min(section.Misc_VirtualSize, section.SizeOfRawData))
     762  
     763  
     764  def call_systemd_measure(uki: UKI, opts: UkifyConfig, profile_start: int = 0) -> str:
     765      measure_tool = find_tool(
     766          'systemd-measure',
     767          '/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-measure',
     768          opts=opts,
     769      )
     770      combined = ''
     771  
     772      banks = opts.pcr_banks or ()
     773  
     774      # PCR measurement
     775  
     776      # First, pick up either the base sections or the profile specific sections we shall measure now
     777      unique_to_measure = {
     778          s.name: s for s in uki.sections[profile_start:] if s.measure and s.name != '.dtbauto'
     779      }
     780  
     781      dtbauto_to_measure: list[Optional[Section]] = [
     782          s for s in uki.sections[profile_start:] if s.measure and s.name == '.dtbauto'
     783      ]
     784  
     785      if len(dtbauto_to_measure) == 0:
     786          dtbauto_to_measure = [None]
     787  
     788      # Then, if we're measuring a profile, lookup the missing sections from the base image.
     789      if profile_start != 0:
     790          for section in uki.sections:
     791              # If we reach the first .profile section the base is over
     792              if section.name == '.profile':
     793                  break
     794  
     795              # Only some sections are measured
     796              if not section.measure:
     797                  continue
     798  
     799              # Check if this is a section we already covered above
     800              if section.name in unique_to_measure:
     801                  continue
     802  
     803              unique_to_measure[section.name] = section
     804  
     805      if opts.measure or opts.policy_digest:
     806          pcrsigs = []
     807          to_measure = unique_to_measure.copy()
     808  
     809          for dtbauto in dtbauto_to_measure:
     810              if dtbauto is not None:
     811                  to_measure[dtbauto.name] = dtbauto
     812  
     813              pp_groups = opts.phase_path_groups or []
     814  
     815              cmd = [
     816                  measure_tool,
     817                  'calculate' if opts.measure else 'policy-digest',
     818                  '--json',
     819                  opts.json,
     820                  *(f'--{s.name.removeprefix(".")}={s.content}' for s in to_measure.values()),
     821                  *(f'--bank={bank}' for bank in banks),
     822                  # For measurement, the keys are not relevant, so we can lump all the phase paths
     823                  # into one call to systemd-measure calculate.
     824                  *(f'--phase={phase_path}' for phase_path in itertools.chain.from_iterable(pp_groups)),
     825              ]
     826  
     827              # The JSON object will be used for offline signing, include the public key
     828              # so that the fingerprint is included too. In case a certificate is passed, use the
     829              # right parameter so that systemd-measure can extract the public key from it.
     830              if opts.policy_digest:
     831                  if opts.pcr_public_keys:
     832                      cmd += ['--public-key', opts.pcr_public_keys[0]]
     833                  elif opts.pcr_certificates:
     834                      cmd += ['--certificate', opts.pcr_certificates[0]]
     835                      if opts.certificate_provider:
     836                          cmd += ['--certificate-source', f'provider:{opts.certificate_provider}']
     837  
     838              print('+', shell_join(cmd), file=sys.stderr)
     839              output = subprocess.check_output(cmd, text=True)  # type: ignore
     840  
     841              if opts.policy_digest:
     842                  pcrsig = json.loads(output)
     843                  pcrsigs += [pcrsig]
     844              else:
     845                  print(output)
     846  
     847          if opts.policy_digest:
     848              combined = combine_signatures(pcrsigs)
     849              # We need to ensure the section has space for signatures, that will be added separately later,
     850              # so add some whitespace to pad the section. At most we'll need 4kb per digest (rsa4096).
     851              # We might even check the key type given we have it to know the precise length, but don't
     852              # bother for now.
     853              combined += ' ' * 1024 * combined.count('"pol":')
     854              uki.add_section(Section.create('.pcrsig', combined))
     855  
     856      # PCR signing
     857  
     858      if opts.pcr_private_keys:
     859          pcrsigs = []
     860          to_measure = unique_to_measure.copy()
     861  
     862          for dtbauto in dtbauto_to_measure:
     863              if dtbauto is not None:
     864                  to_measure[dtbauto.name] = dtbauto
     865  
     866              cmd = [
     867                  measure_tool,
     868                  'sign',
     869                  *(f'--{s.name.removeprefix(".")}={s.content}' for s in to_measure.values()),
     870                  *(f'--bank={bank}' for bank in banks),
     871              ]
     872  
     873              for priv_key, pub_key, cert, group in key_path_groups(opts):
     874                  extra = [f'--private-key={priv_key}']
     875                  if opts.signing_engine is not None:
     876                      assert pub_key or cert
     877                      # Backward compatibility, we used to pass the public key as the certificate
     878                      # as there was no --pcr-certificate= parameter
     879                      extra += [
     880                          f'--private-key-source=engine:{opts.signing_engine}',
     881                          f'--certificate={pub_key or cert}',
     882                      ]
     883                  elif opts.signing_provider is not None:
     884                      assert pub_key or cert
     885                      extra += [
     886                          f'--private-key-source=provider:{opts.signing_provider}',
     887                          f'--certificate={pub_key or cert}',
     888                      ]
     889                  elif cert:
     890                      extra += [f'--certificate={cert}']
     891                  elif pub_key:
     892                      extra += [f'--public-key={pub_key}']
     893  
     894                  if opts.certificate_provider is not None:
     895                      extra += [f'--certificate-source=provider:{opts.certificate_provider}']
     896  
     897                  extra += [f'--phase={phase_path}' for phase_path in group or ()]
     898  
     899                  print('+', shell_join(cmd + extra), file=sys.stderr)  # type: ignore
     900                  output = subprocess.check_output(cmd + extra, text=True)  # type: ignore
     901                  pcrsig = json.loads(output)
     902                  pcrsigs += [pcrsig]
     903  
     904          combined = combine_signatures(pcrsigs)
     905          uki.add_section(Section.create('.pcrsig', combined))
     906  
     907      return combined
     908  
     909  
     910  def join_initrds(initrds: list[Path]) -> Union[Path, bytes, None]:
     911      if not initrds:
     912          return None
     913      if len(initrds) == 1:
     914          return initrds[0]
     915  
     916      seq = []
     917      for file in initrds:
     918          initrd = file.read_bytes()
     919          n = len(initrd)
     920          padding = b'\0' * (round_up(n, 4) - n)  # pad to 32 bit alignment
     921          seq += [initrd, padding]
     922  
     923      return b''.join(seq)
     924  
     925  
     926  T = TypeVar('T')
     927  
     928  
     929  def pairwise(iterable: Iterable[T]) -> Iterator[tuple[T, Optional[T]]]:
     930      a, b = itertools.tee(iterable)
     931      next(b, None)
     932      return zip(a, b)
     933  
     934  
     935  class PEError(Exception):
     936      pass
     937  
     938  
     939  def pe_add_sections(opts: UkifyConfig, uki: UKI, output: str) -> None:
     940      pe = pefile.PE(uki.executable, fast_load=True)
     941  
     942      # Old stubs do not have the symbol/string table stripped, even though image files should not have one.
     943      if symbol_table := pe.FILE_HEADER.PointerToSymbolTable:
     944          symbol_table_size = 18 * pe.FILE_HEADER.NumberOfSymbols
     945          if string_table_size := pe.get_dword_from_offset(symbol_table + symbol_table_size):
     946              symbol_table_size += string_table_size
     947  
     948          # Let's be safe and only strip it if it's at the end of the file.
     949          if symbol_table + symbol_table_size == len(pe.__data__):
     950              pe.__data__ = pe.__data__[:symbol_table]
     951              pe.FILE_HEADER.PointerToSymbolTable = 0
     952              pe.FILE_HEADER.NumberOfSymbols = 0
     953              pe.FILE_HEADER.IMAGE_FILE_LOCAL_SYMS_STRIPPED = True
     954  
     955      # pylint thinks that Structure doesn't have various members that it has…
     956      # pylint: disable=no-member
     957  
     958      # Old stubs might have been stripped, leading to unaligned raw data values, so let's fix them up here.
     959      for i, section in enumerate(pe.sections):
     960          oldp = section.PointerToRawData
     961          oldsz = section.SizeOfRawData
     962          section.PointerToRawData = round_up(oldp, pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.FileAlignment)
     963          section.SizeOfRawData = round_up(oldsz, pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.FileAlignment)
     964          padp = section.PointerToRawData - oldp
     965          padsz = section.SizeOfRawData - oldsz
     966  
     967          for later_section in pe.sections[i + 1 :]:
     968              later_section.PointerToRawData += padp + padsz
     969  
     970          pe.__data__ = (
     971              pe.__data__[:oldp]
     972              + bytes(padp)
     973              + pe.__data__[oldp : oldp + oldsz]
     974              + bytes(padsz)
     975              + pe.__data__[oldp + oldsz :]
     976          )
     977  
     978      # We might not have any space to add new sections. Let's try our best to make some space by padding the
     979      # SizeOfHeaders to a multiple of the file alignment. This is safe because the first section's data starts
     980      # at a multiple of the file alignment, so all space before that is unused.
     981      pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.SizeOfHeaders = round_up(
     982          pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.SizeOfHeaders, pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.FileAlignment
     983      )
     984      pe = pefile.PE(data=pe.write(), fast_load=True)
     985  
     986      # pefile has an hardcoded limit of 256MB, which is not enough when building an initrd with large firmware
     987      # files and all kernel modules. See: https://github.com/erocarrera/pefile/issues/396
     988      warnings = pe.get_warnings()
     989      for w in warnings:
     990          if 'VirtualSize is extremely large' in w:
     991              continue
     992          if 'VirtualAddress is beyond' in w:
     993              continue
     994          raise PEError(f'pefile warnings treated as errors: {warnings}')
     995  
     996      # When attaching signatures we are operating on an existing UKI which might be signed
     997      if not opts.pcrsig:
     998          security = pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.DATA_DIRECTORY[
     999              pefile.DIRECTORY_ENTRY['IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_SECURITY']
    1000          ]
    1001          if security.VirtualAddress != 0:
    1002              # We could strip the signatures, but why would anyone sign the stub?
    1003              raise PEError('Stub image is signed, refusing')
    1004  
    1005      # Remember how many sections originate from systemd-stub
    1006      n_original_sections = len(pe.sections)
    1007  
    1008      for section in uki.sections:
    1009          new_section = pefile.SectionStructure(pe.__IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER_format__, pe=pe)
    1010          new_section.__unpack__(b'\0' * new_section.sizeof())
    1011  
    1012          offset = pe.sections[-1].get_file_offset() + new_section.sizeof()
    1013          if offset + new_section.sizeof() > pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.SizeOfHeaders:
    1014              raise PEError(f'Not enough header space to add section {section.name}.')
    1015  
    1016          assert section.content
    1017          data = section.content.read_bytes()
    1018  
    1019          new_section.set_file_offset(offset)
    1020          new_section.Name = section.name.encode()
    1021          new_section.Misc_VirtualSize = len(data)
    1022          # Non-stripped stubs might still have an unaligned symbol table at the end, making their size
    1023          # unaligned, so we make sure to explicitly pad the pointer to new sections to an aligned offset.
    1024          new_section.PointerToRawData = round_up(len(pe.__data__), pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.FileAlignment)
    1025          new_section.SizeOfRawData = round_up(len(data), pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.FileAlignment)
    1026          new_section.VirtualAddress = round_up(
    1027              pe.sections[-1].VirtualAddress + pe.sections[-1].Misc_VirtualSize,
    1028              pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.SectionAlignment,
    1029          )
    1030  
    1031          new_section.IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ = True
    1032          if section.name == '.linux':
    1033              # Old kernels that use EFI handover protocol will be executed inline.
    1034              new_section.IMAGE_SCN_CNT_CODE = True
    1035  
    1036              # Check if the kernel PE has the NX_COMPAT flag set, if not strip it from the UKI as they need
    1037              # to have the same value, otherwise when firmwares start enforcing it, booting will fail.
    1038              # https://microsoft.github.io/mu/WhatAndWhy/enhancedmemoryprotection/
    1039              # https://www.kraxel.org/blog/2023/12/uefi-nx-linux-boot/
    1040              try:
    1041                  inner_pe = pefile.PE(data=data, fast_load=True)
    1042                  nxbit = pefile.DLL_CHARACTERISTICS['IMAGE_DLLCHARACTERISTICS_NX_COMPAT']
    1043                  if not inner_pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.DllCharacteristics & nxbit:
    1044                      pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.DllCharacteristics &= ~nxbit
    1045              except pefile.PEFormatError:
    1046                  # Unit tests build images with bogus data
    1047                  print(f'{section.name} in {uki.executable} is not a valid PE, ignoring', file=sys.stderr)
    1048          else:
    1049              new_section.IMAGE_SCN_CNT_INITIALIZED_DATA = True
    1050  
    1051          # Special case, mostly for .sbat: the stub will already have a .sbat section, but we want to append
    1052          # the one from the kernel to it. It should be small enough to fit in the existing section, so just
    1053          # swap the data.
    1054          for i, s in enumerate(pe.sections[:n_original_sections]):
    1055              if pe_strip_section_name(s.Name) == section.name and section.name != '.dtbauto':
    1056                  if new_section.Misc_VirtualSize > s.SizeOfRawData:
    1057                      raise PEError(
    1058                          f'Not enough space in existing section {section.name} to append new data'
    1059                          f' (need {new_section.Misc_VirtualSize}, have {s.SizeOfRawData})'
    1060                      )
    1061  
    1062                  padding = bytes(s.SizeOfRawData - new_section.Misc_VirtualSize)
    1063                  pe.__data__ = (
    1064                      pe.__data__[: s.PointerToRawData]
    1065                      + data
    1066                      + padding
    1067                      + pe.__data__[pe.sections[i + 1].PointerToRawData :]
    1068                  )
    1069                  s.Misc_VirtualSize = new_section.Misc_VirtualSize
    1070                  break
    1071          else:
    1072              pe.__data__ = (
    1073                  pe.__data__[:]
    1074                  + bytes(new_section.PointerToRawData - len(pe.__data__))
    1075                  + data
    1076                  + bytes(new_section.SizeOfRawData - len(data))
    1077              )
    1078  
    1079              pe.FILE_HEADER.NumberOfSections += 1
    1080              pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.SizeOfInitializedData += new_section.Misc_VirtualSize
    1081              pe.__structures__.append(new_section)
    1082              pe.sections.append(new_section)
    1083  
    1084      # If there is a pre-signed JSON blob, we need to update the existing JSON, by appending the signature to
    1085      # each corresponding digest object. We have built the unsigned UKI with enough space to fit the .sig
    1086      # objects, so we can just replace the new signed JSON in the existing sections.
    1087      if opts.pcrsig:
    1088          signatures = json.loads(str(opts.pcrsig))
    1089          for i, section in enumerate(pe.sections):
    1090              if pe_strip_section_name(section.Name) == '.pcrsig':
    1091                  j = json.loads(
    1092                      bytes(
    1093                          pe.__data__[
    1094                              section.PointerToRawData : section.PointerToRawData + section.SizeOfRawData
    1095                          ]
    1096                      )
    1097                      .rstrip(b'\x00')
    1098                      .decode()
    1099                  )
    1100                  for (bank, sigs), (input_bank, input_sigs) in itertools.product(
    1101                      j.items(), signatures.items()
    1102                  ):
    1103                      if input_bank != bank:
    1104                          continue
    1105                      for sig, input_sig in itertools.product(sigs, input_sigs):
    1106                          if sig['pol'] == input_sig['pol']:
    1107                              sig['sig'] = input_sig['sig']
    1108  
    1109                  encoded = json.dumps(j).encode()
    1110                  if len(encoded) > section.SizeOfRawData:
    1111                      raise PEError(
    1112                          f'Not enough space in existing section .pcrsig of size {section.SizeOfRawData} to append new data of size {len(encoded)}'  # noqa: E501
    1113                      )
    1114                  section.Misc_VirtualSize = len(encoded)
    1115                  # bytes(n) results in an array of n zeroes
    1116                  padding = bytes(section.SizeOfRawData - len(encoded))
    1117                  pe.__data__ = (
    1118                      pe.__data__[: section.PointerToRawData]
    1119                      + encoded
    1120                      + padding
    1121                      + pe.__data__[section.PointerToRawData + section.SizeOfRawData :]
    1122                  )
    1123  
    1124      pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.CheckSum = 0
    1125      pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.SizeOfImage = round_up(
    1126          pe.sections[-1].VirtualAddress + pe.sections[-1].Misc_VirtualSize,
    1127          pe.OPTIONAL_HEADER.SectionAlignment,
    1128      )
    1129  
    1130      pe.write(output)
    1131  
    1132  
    1133  def merge_sbat(input_pe: list[Path], input_text: list[str]) -> str:
    1134      sbat = []
    1135  
    1136      for f in input_pe:
    1137          try:
    1138              pe = pefile.PE(f, fast_load=True)
    1139          except pefile.PEFormatError:
    1140              print(f'{f} is not a valid PE file, not extracting SBAT section.', file=sys.stderr)
    1141              continue
    1142  
    1143          for section in pe.sections:
    1144              if pe_strip_section_name(section.Name) == '.sbat':
    1145                  split = section.get_data().rstrip(b'\x00').decode().splitlines()
    1146                  if not split[0].startswith('sbat,'):
    1147                      print(f'{f} does not contain a valid SBAT section, skipping.', file=sys.stderr)
    1148                      continue
    1149                  # Filter out the sbat line, we'll add it back later, there needs to be only one and it
    1150                  # needs to be first.
    1151                  sbat += split[1:]
    1152  
    1153      for t in input_text:
    1154          if t.startswith('@'):
    1155              t = Path(t[1:]).read_text()
    1156          split = t.splitlines()
    1157          if not split[0].startswith('sbat,'):
    1158              print(f'{t} does not contain a valid SBAT section, skipping.', file=sys.stderr)
    1159              continue
    1160          sbat += split[1:]
    1161  
    1162      return '\n'.join(
    1163          (
    1164              'sbat,1,SBAT Version,sbat,1,https://github.com/rhboot/shim/blob/main/SBAT.md',
    1165              *sbat,
    1166              '',  # an empty line so that we end up with a newline at the end
    1167          )
    1168      )
    1169  
    1170  
    1171  # Keep in sync with Device from src/boot/chid.h
    1172  # uint32_t descriptor, EFI_GUID chid, uint32_t name_offset, uint32_t compatible_offset
    1173  DEVICE_STRUCT_SIZE = 4 + 16 + 4 + 4
    1174  NULL_DEVICE = b'\0' * DEVICE_STRUCT_SIZE
    1175  DEVICE_TYPE_DEVICETREE = 1
    1176  DEVICE_TYPE_UEFI_FW = 2
    1177  
    1178  # Keep in sync with efifirmware.h
    1179  FWHEADERMAGIC = 'feeddead'
    1180  EFIFW_HEADER_SIZE = 4 + 4 + 4 + 4
    1181  
    1182  
    1183  def device_make_descriptor(device_type: int, size: int) -> int:
    1184      return (size) | (device_type << 28)
    1185  
    1186  
    1187  def pack_device(
    1188      offsets: dict[str, int], devtype: int, name: str, compatible_or_fwid: str, chids: set[uuid.UUID]
    1189  ) -> bytes:
    1190      data = b''
    1191      descriptor = device_make_descriptor(devtype, DEVICE_STRUCT_SIZE)
    1192      for chid in sorted(chids):
    1193          data += struct.pack('<I', descriptor)
    1194          data += chid.bytes_le
    1195          data += struct.pack('<II', offsets[name], offsets[compatible_or_fwid])
    1196  
    1197      assert len(data) == DEVICE_STRUCT_SIZE * len(chids)
    1198      return data
    1199  
    1200  
    1201  def pack_strings(strings: set[str], base: int) -> tuple[bytes, dict[str, int]]:
    1202      blob = b''
    1203      offsets = {}
    1204  
    1205      for string in sorted(strings):
    1206          offsets[string] = base + len(blob)
    1207          blob += string.encode('utf-8') + b'\00'
    1208  
    1209      return (blob, offsets)
    1210  
    1211  
    1212  def parse_hwid_dir(path: Path) -> bytes:
    1213      hwid_files = sorted(path.rglob('*.json'))
    1214      devstr_to_type: dict[str, int] = {
    1215          'devicetree': DEVICE_TYPE_DEVICETREE,
    1216          'uefi-fw': DEVICE_TYPE_UEFI_FW,
    1217      }
    1218  
    1219      # all attributes in the mandatory attributes list must be present
    1220      mandatory_attribute = ['type', 'name', 'hwids']
    1221  
    1222      # at least one of the following attributes must be present
    1223      one_of = ['compatible', 'fwid']
    1224  
    1225      one_of_key_to_devtype: dict[str, int] = {
    1226          'compatible': DEVICE_TYPE_DEVICETREE,
    1227          'fwid': DEVICE_TYPE_UEFI_FW,
    1228      }
    1229  
    1230      strings: set[str] = set()
    1231      devices: collections.defaultdict[tuple[int, str, str], set[uuid.UUID]] = collections.defaultdict(set)
    1232  
    1233      for hwid_file in hwid_files:
    1234          data = json.loads(hwid_file.read_text(encoding='UTF-8'))
    1235  
    1236          for k in mandatory_attribute:
    1237              if k not in data:
    1238                  raise ValueError(f'hwid description file "{hwid_file}" does not contain "{k}"')
    1239  
    1240          if not any(key in data for key in one_of):
    1241              required_keys = ','.join(one_of)
    1242              raise ValueError(f'hwid description file "{hwid_file}" must contain one of {required_keys}')
    1243  
    1244          # (devtype, name, compatible/fwid) pair uniquely identifies the device
    1245          devtype = devstr_to_type[data['type']]
    1246  
    1247          for k in one_of:
    1248              if k in data:
    1249                  if one_of_key_to_devtype[k] != devtype:
    1250                      raise ValueError(
    1251                          f'wrong attribute "{k}" for hwid description file "{hwid_file}", '
    1252                          'device type: "%s"' % devtype
    1253                      )
    1254                  strings |= {data['name'], data[k]}
    1255                  devices[(devtype, data['name'], data[k])] |= {uuid.UUID(u) for u in data['hwids']}
    1256  
    1257      total_device_structs = 1
    1258      for dev, uuids in devices.items():
    1259          total_device_structs += len(uuids)
    1260  
    1261      strings_blob, offsets = pack_strings(strings, total_device_structs * DEVICE_STRUCT_SIZE)
    1262  
    1263      devices_blob = b''
    1264      for (devtype, name, compatible_or_fwid), uuids in devices.items():
    1265          devices_blob += pack_device(offsets, devtype, name, compatible_or_fwid, uuids)
    1266  
    1267      devices_blob += NULL_DEVICE
    1268  
    1269      return devices_blob + strings_blob
    1270  
    1271  
    1272  def parse_efifw_dir(path: Path) -> bytes:
    1273      if not path.is_dir():
    1274          raise ValueError(f'{path} is not a directory or it does not exist')
    1275  
    1276      # only one firmware image must be present in the directory
    1277      # to uniquely identify that firmware with its ID.
    1278      if len(list(path.glob('*'))) != 1:
    1279          raise ValueError(f'{path} must contain exactly one firmware image file')
    1280  
    1281      payload_blob = b''
    1282      for fw in path.iterdir():
    1283          payload_blob += fw.read_bytes()
    1284  
    1285      payload_len = len(payload_blob)
    1286      if payload_len == 0:
    1287          raise ValueError(f'{fw} is a zero byte file!')
    1288  
    1289      dirname = path.parts[-1]
    1290      # firmware id is the name of the directory the firmware bundle is in,
    1291      # terminated by NULL.
    1292      fwid = b'' + dirname.encode() + b'\0'
    1293      fwid_len = len(fwid)
    1294      magic = bytes.fromhex(FWHEADERMAGIC)
    1295  
    1296      efifw_header_blob = b''
    1297      efifw_header_blob += struct.pack('<p', magic)
    1298      efifw_header_blob += struct.pack('<I', EFIFW_HEADER_SIZE)
    1299      efifw_header_blob += struct.pack('<I', fwid_len)
    1300      efifw_header_blob += struct.pack('<I', payload_len)
    1301  
    1302      efifw_blob = b''
    1303      efifw_blob += efifw_header_blob + fwid + payload_blob
    1304  
    1305      return efifw_blob
    1306  
    1307  
    1308  STUB_SBAT = """\
    1309  sbat,1,SBAT Version,sbat,1,https://github.com/rhboot/shim/blob/main/SBAT.md
    1310  uki,1,UKI,uki,1,https://uapi-group.org/specifications/specs/unified_kernel_image/
    1311  """
    1312  
    1313  ADDON_SBAT = """\
    1314  sbat,1,SBAT Version,sbat,1,https://github.com/rhboot/shim/blob/main/SBAT.md
    1315  uki-addon,1,UKI Addon,addon,1,https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-stub.html
    1316  """
    1317  
    1318  
    1319  def make_uki(opts: UkifyConfig) -> None:
    1320      assert opts.output is not None
    1321  
    1322      # kernel payload signing
    1323  
    1324      sign_args_present = opts.sb_key or opts.sb_cert_name
    1325      sign_kernel = opts.sign_kernel
    1326      linux = opts.linux
    1327      combined_sigs = '{}'
    1328  
    1329      # On some distros, on some architectures, the vmlinuz is a gzip file, so we need to decompress it
    1330      # if it's not a valid PE file, as it will fail to be booted by the firmware.
    1331      if linux:
    1332          try:
    1333              pefile.PE(linux, fast_load=True)
    1334          except pefile.PEFormatError:
    1335              try:
    1336                  decompressed = maybe_decompress(linux)
    1337              except NotImplementedError:
    1338                  print(f'{linux} is not a valid PE file and cannot be decompressed either', file=sys.stderr)
    1339              else:
    1340                  print(f'{linux} is compressed and cannot be loaded by UEFI, decompressing', file=sys.stderr)
    1341                  linux = Path(tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(prefix='linux-decompressed').name)
    1342                  linux.write_bytes(decompressed)
    1343  
    1344      if linux and sign_args_present:
    1345          assert opts.signtool is not None
    1346          signtool = SignTool.from_string(opts.signtool)
    1347  
    1348          if sign_kernel is None:
    1349              # figure out if we should sign the kernel
    1350              sign_kernel = signtool.verify(linux, opts)
    1351  
    1352          if sign_kernel:
    1353              linux_signed = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(prefix='linux-signed')
    1354              signtool.sign(os.fspath(linux), os.fspath(Path(linux_signed.name)), opts=opts)
    1355              linux = Path(linux_signed.name)
    1356  
    1357      if opts.uname is None and linux is not None:
    1358          print('Kernel version not specified, starting autodetection 😖.', file=sys.stderr)
    1359          opts.uname = Uname.scrape(linux, opts=opts)
    1360  
    1361      uki = UKI(opts.join_pcrsig if opts.join_pcrsig else opts.stub)
    1362      initrd = join_initrds(opts.initrd)
    1363  
    1364      pcrpkey: Union[bytes, Path, None] = opts.pcrpkey
    1365      if pcrpkey is None:
    1366          keyutil_tool = find_tool('systemd-keyutil', '/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-keyutil')
    1367          cmd = [keyutil_tool, 'extract-public']
    1368  
    1369          if opts.pcr_public_keys and len(opts.pcr_public_keys) == 1:
    1370              # If we're using an engine or provider, the public key will be an X.509 certificate.
    1371              if opts.signing_engine or opts.signing_provider:
    1372                  cmd += ['--certificate', opts.pcr_public_keys[0]]
    1373                  if opts.certificate_provider:
    1374                      cmd += ['--certificate-source', f'provider:{opts.certificate_provider}']
    1375  
    1376                  print('+', shell_join(cmd), file=sys.stderr)
    1377                  pcrpkey = subprocess.check_output(cmd)
    1378              else:
    1379                  pcrpkey = Path(opts.pcr_public_keys[0])
    1380          elif opts.pcr_certificates and len(opts.pcr_certificates) == 1:
    1381              cmd += ['--certificate', opts.pcr_certificates[0]]
    1382              if opts.certificate_provider:
    1383                  cmd += ['--certificate-source', f'provider:{opts.certificate_provider}']
    1384  
    1385              print('+', shell_join(cmd), file=sys.stderr)
    1386              pcrpkey = subprocess.check_output(cmd)
    1387          elif opts.pcr_private_keys and len(opts.pcr_private_keys) == 1:
    1388              cmd += ['--private-key', Path(opts.pcr_private_keys[0])]
    1389  
    1390              if opts.signing_engine:
    1391                  cmd += ['--private-key-source', f'engine:{opts.signing_engine}']
    1392              if opts.signing_provider:
    1393                  cmd += ['--private-key-source', f'provider:{opts.signing_provider}']
    1394  
    1395              print('+', shell_join(cmd), file=sys.stderr)
    1396              pcrpkey = subprocess.check_output(cmd)
    1397  
    1398      hwids = None
    1399  
    1400      if opts.hwids != '':
    1401          if opts.hwids is not None:
    1402              hwids = parse_hwid_dir(Path(opts.hwids))
    1403          else:
    1404              hwids_dir = Path(f'/tmp/s/usr/lib/systemd/boot/hwids/{opts.efi_arch}')
    1405              if hwids_dir.is_dir():
    1406                  print(f'Automatically building .hwids section from {hwids_dir}', file=sys.stderr)
    1407                  hwids = parse_hwid_dir(hwids_dir)
    1408  
    1409      sections = [
    1410          # name,      content,         measure?
    1411          ('.osrel',   opts.os_release, True),
    1412          ('.cmdline', opts.cmdline,    True),
    1413          ('.dtb',     opts.devicetree, True),
    1414          *(('.dtbauto', dtb, True) for dtb in opts.devicetree_auto),
    1415          ('.hwids',   hwids,           True),
    1416          ('.uname',   opts.uname,      True),
    1417          ('.splash',  opts.splash,     True),
    1418          ('.pcrpkey', pcrpkey,         True),
    1419          ('.linux',   linux,           True),
    1420          ('.initrd',  initrd,          True),
    1421          *(('.efifw', parse_efifw_dir(fw), False) for fw in opts.efifw),
    1422          ('.ucode',   opts.microcode,  True),
    1423      ]  # fmt: skip
    1424  
    1425      # If we're building a PE profile binary, the ".profile" section has to be the first one.
    1426      if opts.profile and not opts.join_profiles:
    1427          uki.add_section(Section.create('.profile', opts.profile, measure=True))
    1428  
    1429      for name, content, measure in sections:
    1430          if content:
    1431              uki.add_section(Section.create(name, content, measure=measure))
    1432  
    1433      # systemd-measure doesn't know about those extra sections
    1434      for section in opts.sections:
    1435          uki.add_section(section)
    1436  
    1437      # Don't add an .sbat section to profile PE binaries.
    1438      if (opts.join_profiles or not opts.profile) and not opts.pcrsig:
    1439          if linux is not None:
    1440              # Merge the .sbat sections from stub, kernel, and parameter, so
    1441              # that revocation can be done on either.
    1442              input_pes = [opts.stub, linux]
    1443              if not opts.sbat:
    1444                  opts.sbat = [STUB_SBAT]
    1445          else:
    1446              # Addons don't use the stub so we add SBAT manually
    1447              input_pes = []
    1448              if not opts.sbat:
    1449                  opts.sbat = [ADDON_SBAT]
    1450          uki.add_section(Section.create('.sbat', merge_sbat(input_pes, opts.sbat), measure=linux is not None))
    1451  
    1452      # If we're building a UKI with additional profiles, the .profile section for the base profile has to be
    1453      # the last one so that everything before it is shared between profiles. The only thing we don't share
    1454      # between profiles is the .pcrsig section which is appended later and doesn't make sense to share.
    1455      if opts.profile and opts.join_profiles:
    1456          uki.add_section(Section.create('.profile', opts.profile, measure=True))
    1457  
    1458      # PCR measurement and signing
    1459  
    1460      if (
    1461          not opts.pcrsig
    1462          and (opts.join_profiles or not opts.profile)
    1463          and (
    1464              not opts.sign_profiles
    1465              or (opts.profile and read_env_file(opts.profile).get('ID') in opts.sign_profiles)
    1466          )
    1467      ):
    1468          combined_sigs = call_systemd_measure(uki, opts=opts)
    1469  
    1470      # UKI profiles
    1471  
    1472      to_import = {
    1473          '.linux',
    1474          '.osrel',
    1475          '.cmdline',
    1476          '.initrd',
    1477          '.efifw',
    1478          '.ucode',
    1479          '.splash',
    1480          '.dtb',
    1481          '.uname',
    1482          '.sbat',
    1483          '.profile',
    1484      }
    1485  
    1486      if not opts.os_release:
    1487          to_import.remove('.osrel')
    1488  
    1489      for profile in opts.join_profiles:
    1490          pe = pefile.PE(profile, fast_load=True)
    1491          prev_len = len(uki.sections)
    1492  
    1493          names = [pe_strip_section_name(s.Name) for s in pe.sections]
    1494          names = [n for n in names if n in to_import]
    1495  
    1496          if len(names) == 0:
    1497              raise ValueError(f'Found no valid sections in PE profile binary {profile}')
    1498  
    1499          if names[0] != '.profile':
    1500              raise ValueError(
    1501                  f'Expected .profile section as first valid section in PE profile binary {profile} but got {names[0]}'  # noqa: E501
    1502              )
    1503  
    1504          if names.count('.profile') > 1:
    1505              raise ValueError(f'Profile PE binary {profile} contains multiple .profile sections')
    1506  
    1507          for pesection in pe.sections:
    1508              n = pe_strip_section_name(pesection.Name)
    1509  
    1510              if n not in to_import:
    1511                  continue
    1512  
    1513              print(
    1514                  f"Copying section '{n}' from '{profile}': {pe_section_size(pesection)} bytes",
    1515                  file=sys.stderr,
    1516              )
    1517              uki.add_section(
    1518                  Section.create(n, pesection.get_data(length=pe_section_size(pesection)), measure=True)
    1519              )
    1520  
    1521          if opts.sign_profiles:
    1522              pesection = next(s for s in pe.sections if pe_strip_section_name(s.Name) == '.profile')
    1523              id = read_env_file(pesection.get_data(length=pe_section_size(pesection)).decode()).get('ID')
    1524              if not id or id not in opts.sign_profiles:
    1525                  print(f'Not signing expected PCR measurements for "{id}" profile', file=sys.stderr)
    1526                  continue
    1527  
    1528          s = call_systemd_measure(uki, opts=opts, profile_start=prev_len)
    1529          if s:
    1530              combined_sigs = combine_signatures([json.loads(combined_sigs), json.loads(s)])
    1531  
    1532      # UKI creation
    1533  
    1534      if sign_args_present:
    1535          unsigned = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(prefix='uki')
    1536          unsigned_output = unsigned.name
    1537      else:
    1538          unsigned_output = opts.output
    1539  
    1540      pe_add_sections(opts, uki, unsigned_output)
    1541  
    1542      # UKI signing
    1543  
    1544      if sign_args_present:
    1545          assert opts.signtool is not None
    1546          signtool = SignTool.from_string(opts.signtool)
    1547  
    1548          signtool.sign(os.fspath(unsigned_output), os.fspath(opts.output), opts)
    1549  
    1550          # We end up with no executable bits, let's reapply them
    1551          os.umask(umask := os.umask(0))
    1552          os.chmod(opts.output, 0o777 & ~umask)
    1553  
    1554      print(f'Wrote {"signed" if sign_args_present else "unsigned"} {opts.output}', file=sys.stderr)
    1555      if opts.policy_digest:
    1556          print(combined_sigs)
    1557  
    1558  
    1559  @contextlib.contextmanager
    1560  def temporary_umask(mask: int) -> Iterator[None]:
    1561      # Drop <mask> bits from umask
    1562      old = os.umask(0)
    1563      os.umask(old | mask)
    1564      try:
    1565          yield
    1566      finally:
    1567          os.umask(old)
    1568  
    1569  
    1570  def generate_key_cert_pair(
    1571      common_name: str,
    1572      valid_days: int,
    1573      keylength: int = 2048,
    1574  ) -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
    1575      from cryptography import x509
    1576      from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes, serialization
    1577      from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa
    1578  
    1579      # We use a keylength of 2048 bits. That is what Microsoft documents as
    1580      # supported/expected:
    1581      # https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/windows-secure-boot-key-creation-and-management-guidance?view=windows-11#12-public-key-cryptography
    1582  
    1583      now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
    1584  
    1585      key = rsa.generate_private_key(
    1586          public_exponent=65537,
    1587          key_size=keylength,
    1588      )
    1589      cert = (
    1590          x509.CertificateBuilder()
    1591          .subject_name(
    1592              x509.Name([x509.NameAttribute(x509.oid.NameOID.COMMON_NAME, common_name)]),
    1593          )
    1594          .issuer_name(
    1595              x509.Name([x509.NameAttribute(x509.oid.NameOID.COMMON_NAME, common_name)]),
    1596          )
    1597          .not_valid_before(
    1598              now,
    1599          )
    1600          .not_valid_after(
    1601              now + datetime.timedelta(days=valid_days),
    1602          )
    1603          .serial_number(
    1604              x509.random_serial_number(),
    1605          )
    1606          .public_key(
    1607              key.public_key(),
    1608          )
    1609          .add_extension(
    1610              x509.BasicConstraints(ca=False, path_length=None),
    1611              critical=True,
    1612          )
    1613          .sign(
    1614              private_key=key,
    1615              algorithm=hashes.SHA256(),
    1616          )
    1617      )
    1618  
    1619      cert_pem = cert.public_bytes(
    1620          encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,
    1621      )
    1622      key_pem = key.private_bytes(
    1623          encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,
    1624          format=serialization.PrivateFormat.TraditionalOpenSSL,
    1625          encryption_algorithm=serialization.NoEncryption(),
    1626      )
    1627  
    1628      return key_pem, cert_pem
    1629  
    1630  
    1631  def generate_priv_pub_key_pair(keylength: int = 2048) -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
    1632      from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
    1633      from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa
    1634  
    1635      key = rsa.generate_private_key(
    1636          public_exponent=65537,
    1637          key_size=keylength,
    1638      )
    1639      priv_key_pem = key.private_bytes(
    1640          encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,
    1641          format=serialization.PrivateFormat.TraditionalOpenSSL,
    1642          encryption_algorithm=serialization.NoEncryption(),
    1643      )
    1644      pub_key_pem = key.public_key().public_bytes(
    1645          encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,
    1646          format=serialization.PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo,
    1647      )
    1648  
    1649      return priv_key_pem, pub_key_pem
    1650  
    1651  
    1652  def generate_keys(opts: UkifyConfig) -> None:
    1653      work = False
    1654  
    1655      # This will generate keys and certificates and write them to the paths that
    1656      # are specified as input paths.
    1657      if opts.sb_key and opts.sb_cert:
    1658          fqdn = socket.getfqdn()
    1659  
    1660          cn = f'SecureBoot signing key on host {fqdn}'
    1661          if len(cn) > 64:
    1662              # The length of CN must not exceed 64 bytes
    1663              cn = cn[:61] + '...'
    1664  
    1665          key_pem, cert_pem = generate_key_cert_pair(
    1666              common_name=cn,
    1667              valid_days=opts.sb_cert_validity,
    1668          )
    1669          print(f'Writing SecureBoot private key to {opts.sb_key}', file=sys.stderr)
    1670          with temporary_umask(0o077):
    1671              Path(opts.sb_key).write_bytes(key_pem)
    1672          print(f'Writing SecureBoot certificate to {opts.sb_cert}', file=sys.stderr)
    1673          Path(opts.sb_cert).write_bytes(cert_pem)
    1674  
    1675          work = True
    1676  
    1677      for priv_key, pub_key, _, _ in key_path_groups(opts):
    1678          priv_key_pem, pub_key_pem = generate_priv_pub_key_pair()
    1679  
    1680          print(f'Writing private key for PCR signing to {priv_key}', file=sys.stderr)
    1681          with temporary_umask(0o077):
    1682              Path(priv_key).write_bytes(priv_key_pem)
    1683          if pub_key:
    1684              print(f'Writing public key for PCR signing to {pub_key}', file=sys.stderr)
    1685              Path(pub_key).write_bytes(pub_key_pem)
    1686  
    1687          work = True
    1688  
    1689      if not work:
    1690          raise ValueError(
    1691              'genkey: --secureboot-private-key=/--secureboot-certificate= or --pcr-private-key/--pcr-public-key must be specified'  # noqa: E501
    1692          )
    1693  
    1694  
    1695  def inspect_section(
    1696      opts: UkifyConfig,
    1697      section: pefile.SectionStructure,
    1698  ) -> tuple[str, Optional[dict[str, Union[int, str]]]]:
    1699      name = pe_strip_section_name(section.Name)
    1700  
    1701      # find the config for this section in opts and whether to show it
    1702      config = opts.sections_by_name.get(name, None)
    1703      show = config or opts.all or (name in DEFAULT_SECTIONS_TO_SHOW and not opts.sections)
    1704      if not show:
    1705          return name, None
    1706  
    1707      ttype = config.output_mode if config else DEFAULT_SECTIONS_TO_SHOW.get(name, 'binary')
    1708  
    1709      size = pe_section_size(section)
    1710      data = section.get_data(length=size)
    1711      digest = sha256(data).hexdigest()
    1712  
    1713      struct: dict[str, Union[int, str]] = {
    1714          'size': size,
    1715          'sha256': digest,
    1716      }
    1717  
    1718      if ttype == 'text':
    1719          try:
    1720              struct['text'] = data.rstrip(b'\0').replace(b'\0', b'\\0').decode()
    1721          except UnicodeDecodeError as e:
    1722              print(f'Section {name!r} is not valid text: {e}', file=sys.stderr)
    1723              struct['text'] = '(not valid UTF-8)'
    1724  
    1725      if config and config.content:
    1726          assert isinstance(config.content, Path)
    1727          config.content.write_bytes(data)
    1728  
    1729      if opts.json == 'off':
    1730          print(f'{name}:\n  size: {size} bytes\n  sha256: {digest}')
    1731          if ttype == 'text':
    1732              text = textwrap.indent(cast(str, struct['text']).rstrip(), ' ' * 4)
    1733              print(f'  text:\n{text}')
    1734  
    1735      return name, struct
    1736  
    1737  
    1738  def inspect_sections(opts: UkifyConfig) -> None:
    1739      indent = 4 if opts.json == 'pretty' else None
    1740  
    1741      for file in opts.files:
    1742          pe = pefile.PE(file, fast_load=True)
    1743          gen = (inspect_section(opts, section) for section in pe.sections)
    1744          descs = {key: val for (key, val) in gen if val}
    1745          if opts.json != 'off':
    1746              json.dump(descs, sys.stdout, indent=indent)
    1747  
    1748  
    1749  @dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
    1750  class ConfigItem:
    1751      @staticmethod
    1752      def config_list_prepend(
    1753          namespace: argparse.Namespace,
    1754          group: Optional[str],
    1755          dest: str,
    1756          value: Any,
    1757      ) -> None:
    1758          "Prepend value to namespace.<dest>"
    1759  
    1760          assert not group
    1761  
    1762          old = getattr(namespace, dest, [])
    1763          if old is None:
    1764              old = []
    1765          setattr(namespace, dest, value + old)
    1766  
    1767      @staticmethod
    1768      def config_set_if_unset(
    1769          namespace: argparse.Namespace,
    1770          group: Optional[str],
    1771          dest: str,
    1772          value: Any,
    1773      ) -> None:
    1774          "Set namespace.<dest> to value only if it was None"
    1775  
    1776          assert not group
    1777  
    1778          if getattr(namespace, dest) is None:
    1779              setattr(namespace, dest, value)
    1780  
    1781      @staticmethod
    1782      def config_set(
    1783          namespace: argparse.Namespace,
    1784          group: Optional[str],
    1785          dest: str,
    1786          value: Any,
    1787      ) -> None:
    1788          "Set namespace.<dest> to value only if it was None"
    1789  
    1790          assert not group
    1791  
    1792          setattr(namespace, dest, value)
    1793  
    1794      @staticmethod
    1795      def config_set_group(
    1796          namespace: argparse.Namespace,
    1797          group: Optional[str],
    1798          dest: str,
    1799          value: Any,
    1800      ) -> None:
    1801          "Set namespace.<dest>[idx] to value, with idx derived from group"
    1802  
    1803          # pylint: disable=protected-access
    1804          if group not in namespace._groups:
    1805              namespace._groups += [group]
    1806          idx = namespace._groups.index(group)
    1807  
    1808          old = getattr(namespace, dest, None)
    1809          if old is None:
    1810              old = []
    1811          setattr(
    1812              namespace,
    1813              dest,
    1814              old + ([None] * (idx - len(old))) + [value],
    1815          )
    1816  
    1817      @staticmethod
    1818      def parse_boolean(s: str) -> bool:
    1819          "Parse 1/true/yes/y/t/on as true and 0/false/no/n/f/off/None as false"
    1820          s_l = s.lower()
    1821          if s_l in {'1', 'true', 'yes', 'y', 't', 'on'}:
    1822              return True
    1823          if s_l in {'0', 'false', 'no', 'n', 'f', 'off'}:
    1824              return False
    1825          raise ValueError('f"Invalid boolean literal: {s!r}')
    1826  
    1827      # arguments for argparse.ArgumentParser.add_argument()
    1828      name: Union[str, tuple[str, str]]
    1829      dest: Optional[str] = None
    1830      metavar: Optional[str] = None
    1831      type: Optional[Callable[[str], Any]] = None
    1832      nargs: Optional[str] = None
    1833      action: Optional[Union[str, Callable[[str], Any], builtins.type[argparse.Action]]] = None
    1834      default: Any = None
    1835      version: Optional[str] = None
    1836      choices: Optional[tuple[str, ...]] = None
    1837      const: Optional[Any] = None
    1838      help: Optional[str] = None
    1839  
    1840      # metadata for config file parsing
    1841      config_key: Optional[str] = None
    1842      config_push: Callable[[argparse.Namespace, Optional[str], str, Any], None] = config_set_if_unset
    1843  
    1844      def _names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    1845          return self.name if isinstance(self.name, tuple) else (self.name,)
    1846  
    1847      def argparse_dest(self) -> str:
    1848          # It'd be nice if argparse exported this, but I don't see that in the API
    1849          if self.dest:
    1850              return self.dest
    1851          return self._names()[0].lstrip('-').replace('-', '_')
    1852  
    1853      def add_to(self, parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
    1854          kwargs = {
    1855              key: val
    1856              for key in dataclasses.asdict(self)
    1857              if (key not in ('name', 'config_key', 'config_push') and (val := getattr(self, key)) is not None)
    1858          }
    1859          args = self._names()
    1860          parser.add_argument(*args, **kwargs)
    1861  
    1862      def apply_config(
    1863          self,
    1864          namespace: argparse.Namespace,
    1865          section: str,
    1866          group: Optional[str],
    1867          key: str,
    1868          value: Any,
    1869      ) -> None:
    1870          assert f'{section}/{key}' == self.config_key
    1871          dest = self.argparse_dest()
    1872  
    1873          conv: Callable[[str], Any]
    1874          if self.action == argparse.BooleanOptionalAction:
    1875              # We need to handle this case separately: the options are called
    1876              # --foo and --no-foo, and no argument is parsed. But in the config
    1877              # file, we have Foo=yes or Foo=no.
    1878              conv = self.parse_boolean
    1879          elif self.type:
    1880              conv = self.type
    1881          else:
    1882              conv = lambda s: s  # noqa: E731
    1883  
    1884          # This is a bit ugly, but --initrd and --devicetree-auto are the only options
    1885          # with multiple args on the command line and a space-separated list in the
    1886          # config file.
    1887          if self.name in ['--initrd', '--devicetree-auto']:
    1888              value = [conv(v) for v in value.split()]
    1889          else:
    1890              value = conv(value)
    1891  
    1892          self.config_push(namespace, group, dest, value)
    1893  
    1894      def config_example(self) -> tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str], Optional[str]]:
    1895          if not self.config_key:
    1896              return None, None, None
    1897          section_name, key = self.config_key.split('/', 1)
    1898          if section_name.endswith(':'):
    1899              section_name += 'NAME'
    1900          if self.choices:
    1901              value = '|'.join(self.choices)
    1902          else:
    1903              value = self.metavar or self.argparse_dest().upper()
    1904          return (section_name, key, value)
    1905

    2244  def apply_config(namespace: argparse.Namespace, filename: Union[str, Path, None] = None) -> None:

    2249              print(f'Using config file: {filename}', file=sys.stderr)

    2251              # Try to look for a config file then use the first one found.
    2252              for config_dir in DEFAULT_CONFIG_DIRS:
    2253                  filename = Path(config_dir) / DEFAULT_CONFIG_FILE
    2254                  if filename.is_file():
    2255                      # Found a config file, use it.
    2256                      print(f'Using found config file: {filename}', file=sys.stderr)
    2257                      break

    2259                  # No config file specified or found, nothing to do.
    2260                  return

    2262      # Fill in ._groups based on --pcr-public-key=, --pcr-private-key=, and --phases=.
    2263      assert '_groups' not in namespace

    2265      namespace._groups = list(range(n_pcr_priv))  # pylint: disable=protected-access

    2267      cp = configparser.ConfigParser(
    2268          comment_prefixes='#',
    2269          inline_comment_prefixes='#',
    2270          delimiters='=',
    2271          empty_lines_in_values=False,
    2272          interpolation=None,
    2273          strict=False,
    2274      )
    2275      # Do not make keys lowercase
    2276      cp.optionxform = lambda option: option  # type: ignore

    2278      # The API is not great.

    2280      if not read:
    2281          raise OSError(f'Failed to read {filename}')
    2282  
    2283      for section_name, section in cp.items():
    2284          idx = section_name.find(':')
    2285          if idx >= 0:
    2286              section_name, group = section_name[: idx + 1], section_name[idx + 1 :]
    2287              if not section_name or not group:
    2288                  raise ValueError('Section name components cannot be empty')
    2289              if ':' in group:
    2290                  raise ValueError('Section name cannot contain more than one ":"')

    2300  def config_example() -> Iterator[str]:

    2304          if section:

    2307                      yield ''
    2308                  yield f'[{section}]'
    2309                  prev_section = section
    2310              yield f'{key} = {value}'

      93  def guess_efi_arch() -> str:
      94      arch = os.uname().machine
      95  
      96      for glob, mapping in EFI_ARCH_MAP.items():
      97          if fnmatch.fnmatch(arch, glob):
      98              efi_arch, *fallback = mapping
      99              break
     100      else:
     101          raise ValueError(f'Unsupported architecture {arch}')
     102  
     103      # This makes sense only on some architectures, but it also probably doesn't
     104      # hurt on others, so let's just apply the check everywhere.
     105      if fallback:
     106          fw_platform_size = Path('/sys/firmware/efi/fw_platform_size')
     107          try:
     108              size = fw_platform_size.read_text().strip()
     109          except FileNotFoundError:
     110              pass
     111          else:
     112              if int(size) == 32:
     113                  efi_arch = fallback[0]
     114  
     115      # print(f'Host arch {arch!r}, EFI arch {efi_arch!r}')
     116      return efi_arch

     144  def read_env_file(text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
     145      result = {}
     146  
     147      for line in text.splitlines():
     148          line = line.rstrip()
     149          if not line or line.startswith('#'):
     150              continue
     151          if m := re.match(r'([A-Z][A-Z_0-9]+)=(.*)', line):
     152              name, val = m.groups()
     153              if val and val[0] in '"\'':
     154                  val = next(shlex.shlex(val, posix=True))
     155  
     156              result[name] = val
     157          else:
     158              print(f'bad line {line!r}', file=sys.stderr)
     159  
     160      return result

     163  def get_zboot_kernel(f: IO[bytes]) -> bytes:
     164      """Decompress zboot efistub kernel if compressed. Return contents."""
     165      # See linux/drivers/firmware/efi/libstub/Makefile.zboot
     166      # and linux/drivers/firmware/efi/libstub/zboot-header.S
     167  
     168      # 4 bytes at offset 0x08 contain the starting offset of compressed data
     169      f.seek(8)
     170      _start = f.read(4)
     171      start = struct.unpack('<i', _start)[0]
     172  
     173      # Reading 4 bytes from address 0x0c is the size of compressed data,
     174      # but it needs to be corrected according to the compressed type.
     175      f.seek(0xC)
     176      _sizes = f.read(4)
     177      size = struct.unpack('<i', _sizes)[0]
     178  
     179      # Read 6 bytes from address 0x18, which is a nul-terminated
     180      # string representing the compressed type.
     181      f.seek(0x18)
     182      comp_type = f.read(6)
     183      f.seek(start)
     184      if comp_type.startswith(b'gzip'):
     185          gzip = try_import('gzip')
     186          data = f.read(size)
     187          return cast(bytes, gzip.decompress(data))
     188      elif comp_type.startswith(b'lz4'):
     189          lz4 = try_import('lz4.frame', 'lz4')
     190          data = f.read(size)
     191          return cast(bytes, lz4.frame.decompress(data))
     192      elif comp_type.startswith(b'lzma'):
     193          lzma = try_import('lzma')
     194          data = f.read(size)
     195          return cast(bytes, lzma.decompress(data))
     196      elif comp_type.startswith(b'lzo'):
     197          raise NotImplementedError('lzo decompression not implemented')
     198      elif comp_type.startswith(b'xzkern'):
     199          raise NotImplementedError('xzkern decompression not implemented')
     200      elif comp_type.startswith(b'zstd'):
     201          try:
     202              zstd = try_import('compression.zstd')
     203              data = f.read(size)
     204              return cast(bytes, zstd.zstd.ZstdDecompressor().decompress(data))
     205          except ValueError:
     206              zstd = try_import('zstandard')
     207              data = f.read(size)
     208              return cast(bytes, zstd.ZstdDecompressor().stream_reader(data).read())
     209  
     210      raise NotImplementedError(f'unknown compressed type: {comp_type!r}')
     211  
     212  
     213  def maybe_decompress(filename: Union[str, Path]) -> bytes:
     214      """Decompress file if compressed. Return contents."""
     215      f = open(filename, 'rb')
     216      start = f.read(4)
     217      f.seek(0)
     218  
     219      if start.startswith(b'\x7fELF'):
     220          # not compressed
     221          return f.read()
     222  
     223      if start.startswith(b'MZ'):
     224          f.seek(4)
     225          img_type = f.read(4)
     226          if img_type.startswith(b'zimg'):
     227              # zboot efistub kernel
     228              return get_zboot_kernel(f)
     229          else:
     230              # not compressed aarch64 and riscv64
     231              return f.read()
     232  
     233      if start.startswith(b'\x1f\x8b'):
     234          gzip = try_import('gzip')
     235          return cast(bytes, gzip.open(f).read())
     236  
     237      if start.startswith(b'\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd'):
     238          try:
     239              zstd = try_import('compression.zstd')
     240              return cast(bytes, zstd.zstd.ZstdDecompressor().decompress(f.read()))
     241          except ValueError:
     242              zstd = try_import('zstandard')
     243              return cast(bytes, zstd.ZstdDecompressor().stream_reader(f.read()).read())
     244  
     245      if start.startswith(b'\x02\x21\x4c\x18'):
     246          lz4 = try_import('lz4.frame', 'lz4')
     247          return cast(bytes, lz4.frame.decompress(f.read()))
     248  
     249      if start.startswith(b'\x04\x22\x4d\x18'):
     250          print('Newer lz4 stream format detected! This may not boot!', file=sys.stderr)
     251          lz4 = try_import('lz4.frame', 'lz4')
     252          return cast(bytes, lz4.frame.decompress(f.read()))
     253  
     254      if start.startswith(b'\x89LZO'):
     255          # python3-lzo is not packaged for Fedora
     256          raise NotImplementedError('lzo decompression not implemented')
     257  
     258      if start.startswith(b'BZh'):
     259          bz2 = try_import('bz2', 'bzip2')
     260          return cast(bytes, bz2.open(f).read())
     261  
     262      if start.startswith(b'\x5d\x00\x00'):
     263          lzma = try_import('lzma')
     264          return cast(bytes, lzma.open(f).read())
     265  
     266      raise NotImplementedError(f'unknown file format (starts with {start!r})')
     267

     323  class Uname:
     324      # This class is here purely as a namespace for the functions
     325  
     326      VERSION_PATTERN = r'(?P<version>[a-z0-9._+-]+) \([^ )]+\) (?:#.*)'
     327  
     328      NOTES_PATTERN = r'^\s+Linux\s+0x[0-9a-f]+\s+OPEN\n\s+description data: (?P<version>[0-9a-f ]+)\s*$'
     329  
     330      # Linux version 6.0.8-300.fc37.ppc64le (mockbuild@buildvm-ppc64le-03.iad2.fedoraproject.org)
     331      # (gcc (GCC) 12.2.1 20220819 (Red Hat 12.2.1-2), GNU ld version 2.38-24.fc37)
     332      # #1 SMP Fri Nov 11 14:39:11 UTC 2022
     333      TEXT_PATTERN = rb'Linux version (?P<version>\d\.\S+) \('
     334  
     335      @classmethod
     336      def scrape_x86(cls, filename: Path, opts: Optional[UkifyConfig] = None) -> str:
     337          # Based on https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/mkinitcpio/mkinitcpio/-/blob/master/functions#L136
     338          # and https://docs.kernel.org/arch/x86/boot.html#the-real-mode-kernel-header
     339          with open(filename, 'rb') as f:
     340              f.seek(0x202)
     341              magic = f.read(4)
     342              if magic != b'HdrS':
     343                  raise ValueError('Real-Mode Kernel Header magic not found')
     344              f.seek(0x20E)
     345              offset = f.read(1)[0] + f.read(1)[0] * 256  # Pointer to kernel version string
     346              f.seek(0x200 + offset)
     347              text = f.read(128)
     348          text = text.split(b'\0', maxsplit=1)[0]
     349          decoded = text.decode()
     350  
     351          if not (m := re.match(cls.VERSION_PATTERN, decoded)):
     352              raise ValueError(f'Cannot parse version-host-release uname string: {text!r}')
     353          return m.group('version')
     354  
     355      @classmethod
     356      def scrape_elf(cls, filename: Path, opts: Optional[UkifyConfig] = None) -> str:
     357          readelf = find_tool('readelf', opts=opts)
     358  
     359          cmd = [
     360              readelf,
     361              '--notes',
     362              filename,
     363          ]
     364  
     365          print('+', shell_join(cmd), file=sys.stderr)
     366          try:
     367              notes = subprocess.check_output(cmd, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
     368          except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
     369              raise ValueError(e.stderr.strip()) from e
     370  
     371          if not (m := re.search(cls.NOTES_PATTERN, notes, re.MULTILINE)):
     372              raise ValueError('Cannot find Linux version note')
     373  
     374          text = ''.join(chr(int(c, 16)) for c in m.group('version').split())
     375          return text.rstrip('\0')
     376  
     377      @classmethod
     378      def scrape_generic(cls, filename: Path, opts: Optional[UkifyConfig] = None) -> str:
     379          # import libarchive
     380          # libarchive-c fails with
     381          # ArchiveError: Unrecognized archive format (errno=84, retcode=-30, archive_p=94705420454656)
     382  
     383          # Based on https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/mkinitcpio/mkinitcpio/-/blob/master/functions#L209
     384  
     385          text = maybe_decompress(filename)
     386          if not (m := re.search(cls.TEXT_PATTERN, text)):
     387              raise ValueError(f'Cannot find {cls.TEXT_PATTERN!r} in {filename}')
     388  
     389          return m.group('version').decode()
     390  
     391      @classmethod
     392      def scrape(cls, filename: Path, opts: Optional[UkifyConfig] = None) -> Optional[str]:
     393          for func in (cls.scrape_x86, cls.scrape_elf, cls.scrape_generic):
     394              try:
     395                  version = func(filename, opts=opts)
     396                  print(f'Found uname version: {version}', file=sys.stderr)
     397                  return version
     398              except ValueError as e:
     399                  print(str(e), file=sys.stderr)
     400          return None
     401

     423  @dataclasses.dataclass
     424  class Section:
     425      name: str
     426      content: Optional[Path]
     427      tmpfile: Optional[IO[Any]] = None
     428      measure: bool = False
     429      output_mode: Optional[str] = None
     430  
     431      @classmethod
     432      def create(cls, name: str, contents: Union[str, bytes, Path, None], **kwargs: Any) -> 'Section':
     433          if isinstance(contents, (str, bytes)):
     434              mode = 'wt' if isinstance(contents, str) else 'wb'
     435              tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode=mode, prefix=f'tmp{name}')
     436              tmp.write(contents)
     437              tmp.flush()
     438              contents = Path(tmp.name)
     439          else:
     440              tmp = None
     441  
     442          return cls(name, contents, tmpfile=tmp, **kwargs)
     443  
     444      @classmethod
     445      def parse_input(cls, s: str) -> 'Section':
     446          try:
     447              name, contents, *rest = s.split(':')
     448          except ValueError as e:
     449              raise ValueError(f'Cannot parse section spec (name or contents missing): {s!r}') from e
     450          if rest:
     451              raise ValueError(f'Cannot parse section spec (extraneous parameters): {s!r}')
     452  
     453          if contents.startswith('@'):
     454              sec = cls.create(name, Path(contents[1:]))
     455          else:
     456              sec = cls.create(name, contents)
     457  
     458          sec.check_name()
     459          return sec
     460  
     461      @classmethod
     462      def parse_output(cls, s: str) -> 'Section':
     463          if not (m := re.match(r'([a-zA-Z0-9_.]+):(text|binary)(?:@(.+))?', s)):
     464              raise ValueError(f'Cannot parse section spec: {s!r}')
     465  
     466          name, ttype, out = m.groups()
     467          out = Path(out) if out else None
     468  
     469          return cls.create(name, out, output_mode=ttype)
     470  
     471      def check_name(self) -> None:
     472          # PE section names with more than 8 characters are legal, but our stub does
     473          # not support them.
     474          if not self.name.isascii() or not self.name.isprintable():
     475              raise ValueError(f'Bad section name: {self.name!r}')
     476          if len(self.name) > 8:
     477              raise ValueError(f'Section name too long: {self.name!r}')
     478  
     479  
     480  @dataclasses.dataclass
     481  class UKI:
     482      executable: Path
     483      sections: list[Section] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=list, init=False)
     484  
     485      def add_section(self, section: Section) -> None:
     486          start = 0
     487  
     488          # Start search at last .profile section, if there is one
     489          for i, s in enumerate(self.sections):
     490              if s.name == '.profile':
     491                  start = i + 1
     492  
     493          multiple_allowed_sections = ['.dtbauto', '.efifw']
     494          if any(
     495              section.name == s.name for s in self.sections[start:] if s.name not in multiple_allowed_sections
     496          ):
     497              raise ValueError(f'Duplicate section {section.name}')
     498  
     499          self.sections += [section]

     502  class SignTool:
     503      @staticmethod
     504      def sign(input_f: str, output_f: str, opts: UkifyConfig) -> None:
     505          raise NotImplementedError
     506  
     507      @staticmethod
     508      def verify(input_f: Path, opts: UkifyConfig) -> bool:
     509          raise NotImplementedError
     510  
     511      @staticmethod
     512      def from_string(name: str) -> type['SignTool']:
     513          if name == 'pesign':
     514              return PeSign
     515          elif name == 'sbsign':
     516              return SbSign
     517          elif name == 'systemd-sbsign':
     518              return SystemdSbSign
     519          else:
     520              raise ValueError(f'Invalid sign tool: {name!r}')

     523  class PeSign(SignTool):
     524      @staticmethod
     525      def sign(input_f: str, output_f: str, opts: UkifyConfig) -> None:
     526          assert opts.sb_certdir is not None
     527          assert opts.sb_cert_name is not None
     528  
     529          tool = find_tool('pesign', opts=opts, msg='pesign, required for signing, is not installed')
     530          cmd = [
     531              tool,
     532              '-s',
     533              '--force',
     534              '-n', opts.sb_certdir,
     535              '-c', opts.sb_cert_name,
     536              '-i', input_f,
     537              '-o', output_f,
     538          ]  # fmt: skip
     539  
     540          print('+', shell_join(cmd), file=sys.stderr)
     541          subprocess.check_call(cmd)
     542  
     543      @staticmethod
     544      def verify(input_f: Path, opts: UkifyConfig) -> bool:
     545          assert input_f is not None
     546  
     547          tool = find_tool('pesign', opts=opts)
     548          cmd = [tool, '-i', input_f, '-S']
     549  
     550          print('+', shell_join(cmd), file=sys.stderr)
     551          info = subprocess.check_output(cmd, text=True)
     552  
     553          return 'No signatures found.' in info
     554

     556  class SbSign(SignTool):
     557      @staticmethod
     558      def sign(input_f: str, output_f: str, opts: UkifyConfig) -> None:
     559          assert opts.sb_key is not None
     560          assert opts.sb_cert is not None
     561  
     562          tool = find_tool('sbsign', opts=opts, msg='sbsign, required for signing, is not installed')
     563          cmd = [
     564              tool,
     565              '--key', opts.sb_key,
     566              '--cert', opts.sb_cert,
     567              *(['--engine', opts.signing_engine] if opts.signing_engine is not None else []),
     568              input_f,
     569              '--output', output_f,
     570          ]  # fmt: skip
     571  
     572          print('+', shell_join(cmd), file=sys.stderr)
     573          subprocess.check_call(cmd)
     574  
     575      @staticmethod
     576      def verify(input_f: Path, opts: UkifyConfig) -> bool:
     577          assert input_f is not None
     578  
     579          tool = find_tool('sbverify', opts=opts)
     580          cmd = [tool, '--list', input_f]
     581  
     582          print('+', shell_join(cmd), file=sys.stderr)
     583          info = subprocess.check_output(cmd, text=True)
     584  
     585          return 'No signature table present' in info

     588  class SystemdSbSign(SignTool):
     589      @staticmethod
     590      def sign(input_f: str, output_f: str, opts: UkifyConfig) -> None:
     591          assert opts.sb_key is not None
     592          assert opts.sb_cert is not None
     593  
     594          tool = find_tool(
     595              'systemd-sbsign',
     596              '/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-sbsign',

     598              msg='systemd-sbsign, required for signing, is not installed',
     599          )
     600          cmd = [
     601              tool,
     602              "sign",
     603              '--private-key', opts.sb_key,
     604              '--certificate', opts.sb_cert,
     605              *(
     606                  ['--private-key-source', f'engine:{opts.signing_engine}']
     607                  if opts.signing_engine is not None
     608                  else []
     609              ),
     610              *(
     611                  ['--private-key-source', f'provider:{opts.signing_provider}']
     612                  if opts.signing_provider is not None
     613                  else []
     614              ),
     615              *(
     616                  ['--certificate-source', f'provider:{opts.certificate_provider}']
     617                  if opts.certificate_provider is not None
     618                  else []
     619              ),
     620              input_f,
     621              '--output', output_f,
     622          ]  # fmt: skip
     623  
     624          print('+', shell_join(cmd), file=sys.stderr)
     625          subprocess.check_call(cmd)
     626  
     627      @staticmethod
     628      def verify(input_f: Path, opts: UkifyConfig) -> bool:
     629          raise NotImplementedError('systemd-sbsign cannot yet verify if existing PE binaries are signed')

     638  KNOWN_PHASES = (
     639      'enter-initrd',
     640      'leave-initrd',
     641      'sysinit',
     642      'ready',
     643      'shutdown',
     644      'final',
     645  )

     647  
     648  def parse_phase_paths(s: str) -> list[str]:
     649      # Split on commas or whitespace here. Commas might be hard to parse visually.
     650      paths = re.split(r',|\s+', s)
     651  
     652      for path in paths:
     653          for phase in path.split(':'):
     654              if phase not in KNOWN_PHASES:
     655                  raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f'Unknown boot phase {phase!r} ({path=})')
     656  
     657      return paths
